standing.title: The Rocq export names every dictionary atom through a quadratic clash check before its first poll: a 2.5 MB proof of A ⊢ A runs 28 s past --timeout 1s
standing.evidence: `identifiers` (rocq.rs:242-252) runs `while RESERVED.contains(&id.as_str()) || id == lemma || names.contains(&id)` for every atom, where `names` is a Vec: O(atoms²) string comparisons. `write` calls it on `forest.sequent().atom_names()` (560) before the first `flush` (602), the first place `stop` is asked. `ordinary::rocq` does the same (ordinary/rocq.rs:356). The JSON reader keeps dictionary names that no term uses, and the lemma binds them all ('Lemma certificate (A x0 x1 …'). Run in the capped scope on `{"terms":[{"D":0},{"V":0}],"ids":[0,1],"var_dict":["A","x0",…]}`: 20 000 names took 0.17 s, 80 000 names 3.95 s, against 0.02 s for `--format latex`. `linlog prove --jobs 1 --timeout 1s --format rocq --file dict240000.json` (2 528 955 bytes) ran 28.44 s, exit 0, and wrote the whole certificate: the time limit was never asked.
standing.fix: Check clashes against a `HashSet` of the identifiers taken so far, which is linear and gives the same names. Bind only the atoms that the derivation's sequents use: this changes the output only for a sequent whose dictionary holds unused names, which the lock should be checked for. Ask `stop` during the naming, or name the atoms lazily as the script first meets them.

verdicts.evidence: Read core/src/export/rocq.rs:242-252: `while RESERVED.contains(&id.as_str()) || id == lemma || names.contains(&id)` with `names: Vec<String>`, a scan of every earlier name per atom; `write` calls it at :560 on `forest.sequent().atom_names()` before the first `flush` at :602, the first place `stop` is asked; ordinary/rocq.rs:356 does the same. Ran in the capped scope on `{"terms":[{"D":0},{"V":0}],"ids":[0,1],"var_dict":["A","x0",...]}`: `prove --jobs 1 --timeout 1s --format rocq` took 0.20 s for 20 000 names and 4.72 s for 80 000 (exit 0, 549 003 bytes written), against 0.01 s and 0.02 s for `--format latex` on the same files. Four times the names, 24 times the time, and the 1 s time limit never ended it: S1 (a long call that does not poll its stop) and A1 (a superlinear pass) as claimed. The `HashSet` fix gives the same names, so the lock does not change for it.

Read core/src/export/rocq.rs:242-252 (names is a Vec, `names.contains(&id)` per atom: O(n^2)) and :560 (identifiers called before the first flush/stop at :602); ordinary/rocq.rs:356 does the same. Ran the release binary in the capped scope on {"terms":[{"D":0},{"V":0}],"ids":[0,1],"var_dict":["A","x0"..]}: `prove --jobs 1 --timeout 1s --format rocq` took 181 ms at 20 000 names and 2 479 ms at 60 000 names (exit 0, past the 1 s timeout), against 7 ms and 17 ms for `--format latex`. Quadratic growth and the unpolled stop confirmed (A1 and S1: superlinear blow-up with no stop poll).

standing.title: The SVG layout's i64 arithmetic overflows on large style values: a debug build panics, a release build writes width="-96823495355.-824" at exit 0
standing.evidence: `let scale = |millionths: i64| millionths * size / 1_000_000;` (mod.rs:319). In `run`, `advance = i64::from(font.advances.advance(c)) * shape.1` (359), and `position` sums the advances. Every `Style` length is an unchecked `u32` read from JSON or `--style`: `Advances::Fixed(u32)`, `Table`'s values and fallback (font.rs:64-71), `font_size`, `label_size`, `line_height`, the gaps, `margin`, `link_height`, `link_cap`. Run in the capped scope on a 2 888-byte sequent of 499 atoms: `target/audit/debug/linlog seq print --format svg --style 'svg.font.advances={"fixed":4294967295}' --file long.txt` gives `thread 'main' panicked at core/src/export/svg/mod.rs:319:35: attempt to multiply with overflow`. The release binary prints `<svg … width="-96823495355.-824" height="27.2" viewBox="0 0 -6051468459739 1700" …>` and exits 0. `decimal` (437-440) also mishandles a negative value. The same holds in net.rs:54-55 (`ratio * cap.saturating_mul(rx).isqrt()` and `rx * ratio` with `link_height` near `u32::MAX`) and wherever tree.rs and net.rs add these lengths. The net estimate's 'coordinates of up to twelve digits' (net.rs:93-95) also stops being an upper bound.
standing.fix: Validate `Style` at its entry points and refuse lengths past a stated maximum, for example advances and lengths at most 10^6 thousandths of an em and `font_size` at most 10^4, with an error, or clamp them where serde reads them. Then argue at the declarations that no product reaches i64 (S3), or compute in saturating arithmetic. The infallible `svg::sequent`/`two_sided`/`derivation` would need a fallible form to refuse; R50/S16 say to decide that before 0.1.0. Default and preset styles are untouched, so the behaviour lock does not change.

Ran in the capped scope on a tensor sequent of 499 atoms: `target/audit/debug/linlog seq print --format svg --style 'svg.font.advances={"fixed":4294967295}' --file long.txt` gives `thread 'main' panicked at core/src/export/svg/mod.rs:319:35: attempt to multiply with overflow`; the release binary printed `<svg ... width="35140763122.624" height="27.2" viewBox="0 0 2196297695164 1700" ...>` and exited 0, a wrapped width (my input is shorter than the finding's, so it wrapped to a positive number rather than a negative one; the finding's negative width follows at a longer text). standing.title: Drawing a sequent as SVG takes about 310 bytes per occurrence, with no bound and no stop: a 451-byte JSON sequent takes 2.6 GB under --memory-limit 16MiB
standing.evidence: `svg::sequent` and `svg::two_sided` (mod.rs:525, 535) call `line` (509-521). `line` lays the whole sequent out as one `Run` (`run`, 316-379: a `Piece` struct plus its own `String` for every change of shape, so two per negated atom). It writes every piece into `body`, and `document` (489-505) copies `body` into a second String. Nothing takes a limit or a stop. The only bound is the occurrence limit (default 50 million), and an occurrence costs a few hundred bytes. Shared JSON sequents `{"terms":[{"D":0},{"⅋":[0,0]},…,{"⅋":[k-1,k-1]}],"ids":[k],"var_dict":["a"]}` make this concrete. All runs were in the capped scope with the release binary. k=20 (413 bytes, 2.1 million occurrences): `seq print --format text` peaks at 15 MB, `--format latex` at 21 MB, `--format svg` at 650 MB (205 MB written). k=22 (451 bytes, 8.4 million occurrences): `linlog seq print --memory-limit 16MiB --format svg --file shared22.json` peaked at maxrss 2 589 824 KiB in 2.2 s, exit 0. k=24 (489 bytes, 33.5 million occurrences) is under the default occurrence limit and extrapolates to about 10 GB, past the 4 GiB address space of the planned wasm client. The command's `seq print --format png/pdf` builds the same String before the render's estimate runs. `svg::net` has the same shape: five Strings, then `body`, then the `document` copy (net.rs:272-373), so its peak is about three times the drawing that its `limit` bounds.
standing.fix: Write the line drawing as the tree does. A first pass computes only the width, which the head needs. A second pass writes each piece into any `fmt::Write` as it is laid out: no `Vec<Piece>`, no `body` and no `document` copy. Give `sequent` and `two_sided` a `write(…, out, stop)` form, plus a size bound like `svg::net`'s (an estimate from `occurrences()` times a per-occurrence constant), which the command sets from `--derivation-limit` or `--memory-limit`. Have `svg::net` write its groups straight into the output instead of concatenating and copying. The bytes written stay the same, so the behaviour lock does not change.

Ran in the capped scope on shared20.json (347 bytes, 2^21 − 1 occurrences): `seq print --format text` maxrss 15 212 KiB, `--format latex` 21 400 KiB, `seq print --memory-limit 16MiB --format svg` maxrss 649 852 KiB for a 205 368 064-byte drawing, exit 0; `--format png --memory-limit 16MiB` peaked at the same 649 896 KiB before the render's pixel bound refused it. About 310 bytes per occurrence and three times the drawing, as the finding says; k=22 and k=24 extrapolate to 2.6 GB and 10 GB under the default occurrence limit, which fits the measured k=20. S1 holds: an allocation that grows with the input under no bound the caller can set, where the derivation writers stream.

Read core/src/export/svg/mod.rs:316-379 (run builds a Vec<Piece> with a String per piece), 489-505 (document copies body into a second String), 509-545 (line/sequent/two_sided build drawn, title, run, body, document; no limit or stop). standing.title: The CSR offsets of the net graph are a `u32` of up to three slots per occurrence with no argument or refusal: the cast wraps above 1 431 655 765 occurrences
standing.evidence: `start: Box<[u32]>` ('Per vertex, where its slots start in `to`', graph.rs:39) is filled with `start.push(to.len() as u32)` (:139, :150); `to` gets a parent slot, the children and a literal's axiom slot, up to three per occurrence (:140-148). A forest may hold up to `Forest::MOST` = 2³² − 2 occurrences (`Forest::within(&sequent, limit)`, occurrences/mod.rs:212, and `--occurrence-limit`), so `to.len()` passes `u32::MAX` from 1 431 655 766 occurrences on, where the `as u32` cast wraps silently in a release build and every adjacency `slots` (:169), `axiom_slot` (:174) and the Tarjan search read is wrong, which is the criterion's verdict (`is_correct`, `is_acyclic`) and the net engine's. Unlike `Forest::build` ('add up to no more than a forest can hold', mod.rs:402) and `Pass::readers` (check.rs:864-869), nothing at the declaration says why the number stays in range, and nothing refuses it; the forest it needs takes about 36 GB and the graph 17 GB more, so it is out of reach on this machine but not refused.
standing.fix: Refuse in `ProofStructure::new` a forest of more than a named `nets::MOST` = `u32::MAX / 3` occurrences (an `Error` that names the bound, as `Error::TooManyOccurrences` does), state the argument on `Graph::start`, and pin the arithmetic in a unit test (`3 * MOST + 3 <= u32::MAX as usize`); the alternative, `usize` offsets, doubles the graph's memory for nothing. Behaviour lock: unchanged.

verdicts.evidence: Read core/src/nets/graph.rs:36-44 and 129-155: `start: Box<[u32]>` has no argument at its declaration, and `start.push(to.len() as u32)` (:139, :150) casts with nothing refusing it. `to` gets a parent slot per non-root, two child slots per ⊗/⅋ and an axiom slot per literal (`_ => to.push(NONE)`), so about 2.5 slots per occurrence on average (3 at a binary connective, 2 at a literal). The cast therefore wraps from about 1.72e9 occurrences on, not 1.43e9 as the finding says. That threshold is wrong, but it is still below `Forest::MOST` = 2^32 - 2 (occurrences/mod.rs:195), which `Forest::within` admits (:212, :234). `ProofStructure::new` (nets/mod.rs:202-225) checks the fragment only, and the net engine builds the structure outside the memory account (search/net.rs:227; core-search.md lists the net engine as not counted). This breaks S3 as stated. The fix (refuse above a named bound in `new`, state the argument on `start`) is cheap and leaves the behaviour lock unchanged.

standing.title: A compact view of a chain of affine weakenings (wk) takes quadratic memory and time, past ViewOptions::memory and past the caller's stop
standing.evidence: The compact view handles runs of `?w` in one go (`weaken_run`, :1387), but `Build::weakened` (:1374-1380) returns only `?` weakenings, so a chain of `Node::Weaken` on non-`?` formulas goes node by node: `Weaken(o, p) => { … let up = above(&actual, &[o], &[]); self.from(actual, rule, o, p, up); }` (:1235-1243). `from` (:1172-1181) pushes `Task::Infer { sequent: actual, … }` and then `Task::Unfold(p, up)`, so the descent leaves one pending `Infer` per node on the task stack, each holding its whole conclusion: n²/2 occurrence ids for a chain of n. `Held` (:817-837) counts only inferences already built, never the stack, and the merge in `infer` (:1113-1126) drops those sequents only when the tasks are popped. The stop is polled in `Task::Unfold` only (:1038-1041), so the n pops of `Task::Infer`, each O(n) (`into_vec`, `held.cost` twice, `position`), run without a poll. Measured with the release binary in the capped scope, `prove -a --deterministic --file F` on `|- a, ~a, b0, …, b(n-1)` (the proof is a chain of n `wk`; the full derivation is over the default bounds, so `--compact auto` builds the two-inference compact tree), peak RSS by getrusage: n=10 000 201 MB 0.18 s; n=20 000 776 MB 0.66 s; n=40 000 3 072 MB 2.40 s, against the default memory bound of 1 GiB and a compact budget of 64 MiB, while `--format json` of the same input takes 21 MB and 0.03 s. Pinned to the builder by the `?w` twin, `|- a, ~a, ?b0, …, ?b39999` in classical mode: 26 MB, 0.06 s. The stop: `--timeout 200ms` and `600ms` leave the derivation out at 0.24 s and 0.71 s (the descent is polled), but `--timeout 1s` answers at 2.42 s with the derivation written, exit 0. The time limit was overrun by 1.4 s, all of it spent in the unpolled pops.
standing.fix: Walk a chain of affine weakenings in one go as `weaken_run` does for `?w`: have `weakened` return the rule along with the formula (`Weakening` for a `?` formula, `AffineWeakening` otherwise, after the intuitionistic renaming, since `wk` keeps its name), and have `weaken_run` push one `Task::Infer` with that rule and `times = removed.len()`. Also poll the stop in every task, not only in `Unfold`, so that no tail of `Infer` tasks runs unpolled (with `--derivation-limit none` the non-compact tail is unbounded too). Add a test that builds the compact view of a long `wk` chain within a small `ViewOptions::memory`. The output is unchanged: `infer` already merges the run into the same single inference with the lowest application's principal, so the behaviour lock and the snapshots stay as they are.

standing.title: Reading a session back (Interactive::from_parts) takes quadratic time in the file, with no stop
standing.evidence: By reading; I did not run this one. (1) The history check walks each history entry from the last back and calls `state.subtree(goal)` (line 322, defined at line 796). That collects every inference above the goal, whatever `len` is, before the filter `id < len`. On a chain of n steps, each closing the goal the previous one opened, the walks sum to n²/2. (2) `replay` recovers a split for every closed ⊗ or Mix (lines 372-390). For each member of the left premise it scans the conclusion from position 0 with `sequent.iter().enumerate().position(|(i, &x)| x == o && !used[i])` (line 384). That is O(k²) for a conclusion of k formulas. Both run inside `Deserialize for Interactive` (serialize/interactive.rs:73ff) with no stop. They are reached by `linlog interact --state FILE` and the session's `load` (interact.rs:49, 347), outside any time limit, and they will be reached by the web client, for which this JSON is 'the form a web client holds between requests' (core-sequents.md). The fuzzer's `-max_len` is 16 KB with a 20 s timeout (fuzz/run.sh:51-56), so stage 0's run on json_session could not show superlinear work.
standing.fix: Make both passes linear. For the split, walk the sorted conclusion and the sorted premise context with two pointers. For the history, mark from the last step back only the inferences not yet seen, and stop a walk at an inference already marked or at an index of `len` or more. Each inference is then visited once. Add a test that times, or counts the steps of, a chain session at n and 2n. No change to the behaviour lock.

standing.title: Interactive::apply takes its step as positional arguments, which a witness cannot be added to without a new signature
standing.evidence: `pub fn apply(&mut self, goal: InfId, position: usize, rule: Rule, left: &[usize]) -> Result<Vec<InfId>, Refusal>` (proofs/interactive.rs:538-544). Step 38 needs a witness term or an open metavariable per step and step 36 a split that is a cut position rather than a subset (R96); after 0.1.0 either is a second method beside this one (D18 forbids keeping both), and the command's `apply G P RULE [P…]` grammar (cli/src/interact.rs) and the session JSON are built on the present shape by step 32.

standing.title: `Interactive::close_with` grafts a proof over another forest, or one the session's mode forbids, and reports the session complete (and can panic)
standing.evidence: `close_with` (interactive.rs:840-852) calls `Derivation::of_goal(proof, &sequent, self.mode, …)` which checks the proof against the goal's ids over the proof's own forest (`check::examine(proof, goal, …)`, derivation.rs:777) and in `mode.affine()` (derivation.rs:688); nothing compares `proof.sequent()` with the session's or the mode. Witness (scratchpad/audit/sound-check/graft, `cargo run` against core/ by path): session `A, A -o B |- B` classical, goal [0, 1, 4]; the proof `[Top(4)]` of `|- A, B, C, D, top` checks over its own forest, then `close_with: Ok(())`, `is_complete: true`, `derivation()` draws `⊢ ~A, A ⊗ ~B, B` closed by `⊤`, `proof()` → `invalid proof: node 0 (⊤ on 4): occurrence 4 is not what the rule acts on` (the doc of `proof()` at :946-951 says the checker 'never does [reject] for a derivation built through this interface'), and the session's JSON does not read back (`the rule ⊤ does not act on formula 2`). With the proof `[Top(0)]` of `|- top` (a smaller forest): `panicked at core/src/proofs/size.rs:242:31: index out of bounds: the len is 1 but the index is 1` (`self.weights[o.index()]` over the proof's forest with the session's ids). Second binary `mode`: session `A, B |- A` classical (not affine), proof `[Ax(0,2), Weaken(1, 0)]` over the same forest: `check classical: Err(Forbidden)`, `check affine: Ok(())`, `close_with: Ok(())`, `is_complete: true`, a `wk` inference drawn, `proof()` → `the mode forbids the rule`. Known leftover of step 21 (plan/28-audit-and-refactor.md, 'From step 21'), still as it was. The command's `interact` is not affected (cli/src/interact.rs:379 grafts the proof of its own `prove_goal` over the session's forest).
standing.fix: In `close_with`, refuse a proof whose `sequent()` differs from `self.sequent()` (the forest is a function of the sequent, D5) with an `Error` variant that names it (`Error::InconsistentState` or a new `Error::ForeignProof`), and have `of_goal` check in `self.mode` rather than `mode.affine()` (no engine emits `Weaken` outside affine mode, so `close` is unchanged). Behaviour lock: unchanged (the lock's interactive session uses `close`); the new error is a new variant, not a changed form.

also.evidence: `let found = Derivation::of_goal(proof, &sequent, self.mode, view, &mut stop)?; self.graft(goal, found);` (848-850): of_goal checks the proof against the goal's ids in the proof's own forest, and nothing compares `proof.forest()` with `self.forest`. Probe (scratch crate against the current tree): session `|- 1 par 1`, `apply` ⅋ gives goal [1, 2] (⊢ 1, 1, unprovable without Mix); a proof of the ids [1, 2] from `prove_goal` over the forest of `|- B par ~B`; `close_with` returns `Ok(())`, `is_complete()` is true, `derivation()` prints `────── ax / ⊢ 1, 1 / ─────── ⅋ / ⊢ 1 ⅋ 1`, `proof()` fails `invalid proof: node 0 (ax on 1, 2): occurrence 1 is not what the rule acts on` although its doc says the checker never rejects a derivation built through this interface (949), and the session's own JSON reads back as `Err("the rule ax does not act on formula 0")`.
also.fix: Refuse a proof whose forest is not the session's (compare `proof.forest().sequent()` with `self.forest.sequent()` before `of_goal`, one pass over the arena) with a named error; a test with the probe's two sequents. No change to the behaviour lock (the command grafts only its own proofs).

verdicts.evidence: Read proofs/interactive.rs:840-852. close_with calls `Derivation::of_goal(proof, &sequent, self.mode, …)` and grafts the result, and nothing compares `proof.sequent()`/`proof.forest()` with the session's. derivation.rs:680-691 checks with `mode.affine()`, and :777 `check::examine(proof, goal, …)` reads the proof's own forest. So a proof over another forest whose ids happen to cover the goal is grafted, and a Weaken is accepted in a non-affine session. I read the reviewer's witness programs (scratchpad/audit/sound-check/graft/src/main.rs and bin/mode.rs); both build exactly the cases described, and the code paths above give the results reported. I did not rerun them: building them needs serde_json, which may not be cached offline. The method reports success (`is_complete`) on a wrong state, then `proof()` fails, against its own doc. C-VALIDATE's must-fix applies. The fix leaves the behaviour lock unchanged, since the command grafts over its own forest (cli/src/interact.rs).

Read close_with (interactive.rs:840-852): it takes the goal's ids from the session and calls Derivation::of_goal(proof, &sequent, self.mode, view, &mut stop). of_goal (derivation.rs:683-689) runs check::reading(proof, mode) and unfold(proof, goal, mode.affine(), ...) with the proof's own forest. mode.affine() is the method returning Mode with affine allowed (fragment.rs:247), so a session that is not affine is checked as if it were; the `mode` witness holds. Nothing compares proof.forest() or proof.sequent() with self.forest, and unfold's size pass indexes weights by the session ids over the proof's forest (size.rs:242 per the report), so a smaller forest can panic. close_with is pub, and the leftover is listed in plan/28 'From step 21'. I did not rerun the witnesses; the code path is clear and the public method accepts a foreign proof. Must-fix by C-VALIDATE (invalid argument gives a wrong answer silently) and S5/S11 (panic; the proof() doc contradicted).

standing.title: optimize sorts the roots, so the written order of a sequent is lost before 0.1.0 fixes the canonical form
standing.evidence: `optimize_roots`: `self.roots.sort();` (sequents/mod.rs:205), run by `optimize` (:314-320) after every parse (parse/mod.rs) and by ordinary/translate.rs:441-445, which pairs roots by the sorted term id. Run: `linlog seq print '|- A, B, A'` prints `⊢ A, A, B`; `linlog seq print -i '0, top |- top'` prints `0, 0 ⊢ 0`; `linlog seq print -i '|- A, top'` prints `0 ⊢ A` (the written succedent is lost, R54). Step 36 needs the written order as the canonical form (plan/36-lambek.md:24-27); doing it after 0.1.0 shifts the occurrence ids of every stored proof and session whose roots were not already ascending, a format break (C1, option B). The register leaves the when to the author (C1); the research (research/README.md §3 conflict 2, 36-lambek.md §3) recommends step 28.
standing.fix: Stop sorting in `optimize_roots` (keep its bounds check) so that parse, JSON, `Sequent::add`, Display and `Forest::roots()` keep the roots as written; update ordinary/translate.rs's root pairing; state the canonical form on `Sequent` and in core-sequents.md and core-forest.md, and settle whether a cyclic sequent's equality is up to rotation. This changes the behaviour lock and the snapshots for exactly the inputs whose roots were not ascending (one commit that names them), unless the author chooses option B, in which case the finding becomes a documented versioned break at step 36.

verdicts.evidence: Confirmed at core/src/sequents/mod.rs:203-205 (`self.roots.sort();` in optimize_roots, run by optimize at :314-320). I re-ran the probes with the prebuilt binary under the capped scope. `seq print '|- A, B, A'` gave `⊢ A, A, B`, `seq print -i '0, top |- top'` gave `0, 0 ⊢ 0`, `seq print -i '|- A, top'` gave `0 ⊢ A`, and `seq print '|- A par B, A'` gave `⊢ A, A ⅋ B`, so the written order is lost. R53 lists step 28. Conflict C1 (requirements.md:2103-2111) recommends Option A (stop sorting at step 28, before 0.1.0), and doing it later shifts the occurrence ids of files whose roots were not ascending. Severity: must-fix under S16 if the author takes Option A (or C). Under Option B it becomes a documented versioned break at step 36, as the finding itself states.

Ran `linlog seq print '|- A, B, A'` -> `⊢ A, A, B`; `seq print -i '|- A, top'` -> `0 ⊢ A`; `seq print -i '0, top |- top'` -> `0, 0 ⊢ 0`. sequents/mod.rs:205 `self.roots.sort();` confirmed. standing.title: No JSON form carries a version, so a 0.1.0 reader silently accepts a file written by a later library and drops its new keys
standing.evidence: The proxies struct Proof { sequent, proof } (serialize/proofs.rs:61-67), struct Net { sequent, mix, links } (nets.rs:13-20), struct Interactive { sequent, mode, inferences, history } (interactive.rs:34-43) and struct Sequent { terms, ids, var_dict } (sequents.rs:52-59) have no version key and no deny_unknown_fields (grep -rn 'version|schema' core/src/serialize/ finds nothing). Probe with the prebuilt command: a proof file {"version":2, "sequent":…, "cuts":[1], "proof":[{"ax":[0,1]}]} gives 'valid proof of ⊢ ~A, A (classical)', exit 0: the keys version and cuts were dropped without a word, so a file of step 34 written under its own rule reads on today's reader as a different, valid, cut-free proof. Only a new node tag fails ('unknown variant `cut`'), by serde's wording, never by version. The 2^53 rule (R247) is unwritten: Size writes saturating u64 fields (proofs/size.rs:29-43), WhyNot::Equation.needed is i128 (serialize/search.rs:120). ModeDef (serialize/search.rs:46-55) has no serde(default), so the cyclic flag of R10 breaks the reading of every stored mode object.
standing.fix: Write version: 1 on every top-level form a program reads back (Proof, ProofStructure, Interactive) and on the written Outcome; read a missing version as 1 and refuse a greater one with a message that names it; serde(default) on ModeDef; state the policy once in the crate docs and core-sequents.md (additive keys only, what an unknown key and an unknown tag do, numbers exact below 2^53 with u64::MAX meaning saturated) with a test per form that reads a pre-change fixture and one that refuses version 2. Changes the behaviour lock: every pinned JSON form (core/tests/lock/json.txt, core/tests/serialize.rs, the cli lock's JSON calls, README's JSON blocks) gains the key, in a commit of its own.

also.evidence: None of the proxies has a `version` key or `deny_unknown_fields`: sequents.rs:67 `struct Sequent { terms, ids, var_dict }`, proofs.rs:62 `{ sequent, proof }`, nets.rs:188 `{ sequent, mix, links }`, interactive.rs:34 `{ sequent, mode, inferences, history }`, search.rs:48 ModeDef. Runs with target/audit/release/linlog in the capped scope: (1) `echo '{"sequent":{"terms":[{"D":0},{"V":0}],"ids":[0,1],"var_dict":["A"],"version":7,"fo_terms":[1]},"proof":[{"ax":[0,1]}],"cuts":[3,4],"version":99}' | linlog check` printed `valid proof of ⊢ ~A, A (classical)`, status 0. (2) A session `{"version":2, …, "mode":{"intuitionistic":false,"affine":false,"mix":false,"ordering":"lambek"}, …, "cuts":[7]}` given to `interact --state` printed `goal 0: ⊢ 0: ~A ⅋ ~B, 1: B ⊗ A`: the version, the ordering and the cuts were all dropped, and the session went on in commutative classical mode. Steps 34 (`cuts`, R13/R14), 36 (an ordering in Mode, R10) and 38 (term arena, R16/R17) add exactly such keys. A 0.1.0 reader that does not check a version now cannot be taught to refuse them after the release.
also.fix: Give every form a client stores (Proof, Interactive, ProofStructure, and the new ones) a `version`, read as 1 when absent. A reader refuses a larger one with a named error (`Error::FormatVersion { found, known }`). Write the rule once in the crate docs and core-sequents.md (R6). This changes the behaviour lock once, in a commit of its own: every pinned top-level JSON string in core/tests/lock/json.txt, core/tests/serialize.rs, README and cli/tests/lock/out gains `"version":1`. Putting the key on the top-level forms only, not inside the embedded Sequent, keeps the sequent strings byte-identical.

verdicts.evidence: Confirmed by a probe under the capped scope with target/audit/release/linlog. `prove --format json 'A |- A'` gave a proof, and I rewrote it as {"version":2,"sequent":…,"cuts":[1],"proof":[{"ax":[0,1]}]}. `linlog check` on that file printed 'valid proof of ⊢ ~A, A (classical)', exit 0, dropping both unknown keys silently. The proxies have no version key (serialize/proofs.rs:61-67; serialize/interactive.rs:34-43; serialize/sequents.rs:52-59), and serialize/search.rs:46 ModeDef derives Deserialize with no serde(default). R6 lists step 28, and the step's own goal (plan/28-audit-and-refactor.md:501) asks for 'each JSON form with a version and documented schema'. A version read by a 0.1.0 reader cannot be added afterwards for readers already shipped, which is the AIP-180 must-fix case. Constraint for the fix: deny_unknown_fields on Proof would break `check` reading prove's Outcome JSON, whose proof keys are flattened among the others (core-sequents.md), so the version key, not deny_unknown_fields, is the right mechanism, as proposed.

grep -rn 'version|deny_unknown' core/src/serialize finds nothing. Probe `linlog check` on {"version":2,"sequent":{...},"cuts":[1],"proof":[{"ax":[0,1]}]} printed `valid proof of ⊢ ~A, A (classical)`, exit 0, so version and cuts were silently dropped. ModeDef (serialize/search.rs:46-55) has no serde(default). R6 says each form carries a version or is declared never to need one; neither is done and no unknown-key policy is written (core-sequents.md has none). It is must-fix because a 0.1.0 reader that does not check a version cannot refuse a later file, and that is only fixable before the release. Fix changes the JSON lock (every pinned form gains the key). Includes api-wire-1.

standing.title: A proof file, a session and a proof structure are read within the default 50 million occurrences whatever the caller asks: 457 bytes take 1.48 GB under `check --memory-limit 16MiB`
standing.evidence: proofs.rs:135 `let forest = Forest::try_from(p.sequent)?;`, and the same at nets.rs:219 and interactive.rs:73. `TryFrom<Sequent> for Forest` measures against `Self::DEFAULT_LIMIT` (occurrences/mod.rs:394), and `Interactive::new` calls `Forest::new` (proofs/interactive.rs:215). No public entry reads these forms within another limit. `check` has no `--occurrence-limit` (CheckArgs, cli/src/argument_parsing.rs:453), and `interact --state` reads with plain serde (cli/src/interact.rs:90-93). Measured: a 457-byte proof file whose sequent is a tower of 25 shared ⊗ (33.5 million occurrences), run as `linlog check --memory-limit 16MiB FILE` under a 4G scope on cores 6-15. Result: status 1 after 1.96 s, with a maximum RSS of 1477 MiB (getrusage of the children).
standing.fix: Add a reading entry that takes the limit: a `DeserializeSeed`, or `Proof::from_json_within` / `Interactive::from_json_within` / `ProofStructure::from_json_within`, plus `Interactive::new_within`. The command's `check` and `interact --state` take `--occurrence-limit` through them. Document the default in each type's JSON section. No change to pinned output; `check --help` gains a flag.

also.evidence: Forest::try_from(p.sequent) in serialize/proofs.rs:135, nets.rs:44 and interactive.rs:73, which is Forest::measure(&sequent, Self::DEFAULT_LIMIT) (occurrences/mod.rs:392-394; DEFAULT_LIMIT = 50_000_000 at :191, about 25 bytes each, so 1.25 GB); Interactive::new calls Forest::new(sequent) (proofs/interactive.rs:214-215). The command: 'linlog check --help' lists no --occurrence-limit (probe; CheckArgs at cli/src/argument_parsing.rs:453-472 has memory_limit, proof, mode, output only), and cli.md says of --occurrence-limit 'A session's state and a proof file are read by serde, which takes no options: their sequents are under the default whatever the flag says.' The register's R27 and the research's D-9 ('every Deserialize has a _within twin') put the entry at step 28; a sibling added after 0.1.0 beside new() is the alias S17 forbids.
also.fix: Interactive::new takes the limit (or a Limits value) now; a from_json_within / DeserializeSeed entry for Proof, ProofStructure and Interactive that takes the occurrence limit, used by the command's check and interact --state under --occurrence-limit (add the flag to check), and documented as what a front end calls. No change of the behaviour lock (the defaults stay).

verdicts.evidence: Confirmed. serialize/proofs.rs:135 `let forest = Forest::try_from(p.sequent)?;`, serialize/interactive.rs:73, and serialize/nets.rs:44 (the finding's '219' is off; the duplicate ready-a-4 has :44) all go through TryFrom<Sequent> for Forest, which measures against Self::DEFAULT_LIMIT (occurrences/mod.rs:392-394). Interactive::new calls Forest::new (proofs/interactive.rs:215). CheckArgs (cli/src/argument_parsing.rs:451-470) has no --occurrence-limit, and interact's load is plain serde_json::from_str (cli/src/interact.rs:90-94). .claude/rules/cli.md documents it: 'A session's state and a proof file are read by serde, which takes no options: their sequents are under the default whatever the flag says.' S1 requires an input-sized allocation to be under a bound the caller sets. R27 and the step's own leftovers (plan/28-audit-and-refactor.md:42-44) assign the fix here. I did not rerun the 1.48 GB measurement, but the mechanism is plain in the code: 33.5 M occurrences is under the 50 M default at about 25 B each. A library caller could pre-read the sequent through serde_json::Value and check occurrences(), but the command does not, and the typed readers offer no limit.

serialize/proofs.rs:135, nets.rs:44 and interactive.rs:73 all call Forest::try_from(...), which uses the 50M DEFAULT_LIMIT. Built a 24-level shared-⊗ tower proof file (about 500 bytes, 33.5M occurrences) and ran `linlog check --memory-limit 16MiB FILE` under the capped scope. Result: exit 1, max RSS 1478 MiB (getrusage). `check --help` has no occurrence-limit flag (only a --net line mentions occurrence numbers). standing.title: The error family has no kind: no machine-readable reason, no serializable form, and Error does not tell a refusal from a fault
standing.evidence: `#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error` has no serde and no `is_refusal()` or `kind()`. No error type in the crate implements Serialize: a grep finds serde only on the options values, Size, Rule and the data forms. Refusals (TooManyOccurrences, Unchecked, View(Memory|TooLarge|TooMany|Stopped), NetFragment, NetMode, NetGoal, EngineMode, NotAdditive, NotHorn, IntuitionisticMix) are variants beside faults (InvalidProof, Rejected, InconsistentState, the index errors), so a client must list them. The harness does so by hand at bench/src/run.rs:636-641: it lists six and files TooManyOccurrences and Unchecked, which are refusals by S18's definition, under "error". Payloads are positional or prose: `InvalidVariableIndex(usize, usize)`, `InconsistentState(&'static str)`, `ReadBack { calculus: &'static str, reason: String }`, `Lltp(String)`, `Mist(String)`, `Tptp(String)`. Refusal (proofs/interactive.rs:39), ViewError, NetError, ShapeError and CheckError have no wire form either.
standing.fix: Add `Error::kind()`, returning a `#[non_exhaustive]` enum of stable snake_case codes with `is_refusal()`. Give every payload named fields. Implement Serialize (behind `serialize`) as `{code, message, refusal, details}` from one place, with a test that matches every variant without a wildcard. Refusal, ViewError, NetError, ShapeError and CheckError serialize the same way. standing.title: A refused compact view reports the size of the whole derivation, and the compact view's lower bound is computed and thrown away
standing.evidence: `unfold` computes the compact view's lower bound and drops it. Line 737: `let (size, firm) = size::measured(proof, goal, mode, reading, view.memory)?;`. When a compact view is tried and refused, the error is still the whole derivation's: at :768, `|| most.is_some_and(|most| firm.bytes > most)` leads to `return Err(error)`, where `error` is the `TooLarge { size, limit }` or `Memory { size: Some(size), .. }` built from the whole `size` (:739-751). An attempt that gives up partway through the build ends at :1034 with `return Err(held.budget.error.clone())`, the same error carried by `Budget { most, error }` (:773). The field doc says `size: The derivation's size.` (:450, and the same at :458 for Memory). `size::Firm` is `pub(crate)` (size.rs:146), so no caller can learn the bound. The command's `too_large` (cli/src/prove.rs:539) prints that size. Probe (capped scope): the sequent is 300 `?a_i` and twenty `1` joined by `*` (scratchpad audit/api-surface/gap/seq.txt). `linlog prove --deterministic --compact always --derivation-limit 12KiB --file seq.txt` printed `the derivation is not written: its 339 inferences with 323764 characters of sequents are estimated at 2.5 MiB, over the limit of 12.0 KiB; … --derivation-limit SIZE raises the limit`. With `--derivation-limit 16KiB` the same call writes the compact derivation the user asked for: 40 inferences (20 `1`, 19 `⊗`, one `?w*` run). The line names a derivation that was not asked for and is about 160 times larger. A user who raises the limit to the 2.5 MiB it names overshoots a bound of 16 KiB 160-fold. Under `--compact auto` (the default) the line does not say that a compact view was tried or what it would need.
standing.fix: Where a compact view was tried or asked for, carry its lower bound in the error. Make `Firm` public (for example as `size::Least { inferences, bytes }`) and give `TooLarge` and `Memory` a field `compact: Option<Least>`, which must be added before 0.1.0 since the struct variants are not non_exhaustive. With `Compact::Always`, document `size` as the whole derivation's size and lead with the compact figures. `Display` and the command's `too_large`/`over_memory` would add a clause such as "drawn compact it takes at least N inferences, estimated at B" only where `firm` is smaller than the whole size, which happens only when the derivation has a structural rule. Behaviour lock: unchanged. The pinned left-out lines (README.md:441 and cli/tests/lock/out/format-derivation-limit.txt) are MLL proofs without structural rules, where `firm` equals the whole size and no clause is added. No snapshot pins a refused compact view.

verdicts.evidence: Read core/src/proofs/derivation.rs:737-776: `size::measured` returns `(size, firm)`; `TooLarge`/`Memory` are built from `size` (:739-751); when a compact view is tried, `firm` is used only to decide `return Err(error)` (:768) or to carry the same `error` in `Budget` (:773), which `run` returns at :1034. `Firm` is `pub(crate)` (core/src/proofs/size.rs:146), and `ViewError::TooLarge { size }` is documented as `The derivation's size` (:450). Ran in the capped scope on `|- ?a0, …, ?a299, 1 * … * 1` (twenty `1`): `prove --deterministic --compact always --derivation-limit 12KiB` prints `the derivation is not written: its 339 inferences with 323764 characters of sequents are estimated at 2.5 MiB, over the limit of 12.0 KiB; …`, while `--derivation-limit 16KiB` writes the compact derivation (43 lines, one `?w*` run). The message names a derivation the user did not ask for and gives no figure for the one they did; `--compact auto` prints the same line. Holds under S18/C-INTERMEDIATE as a reader misled.

Read core/src/proofs/derivation.rs:725-790 and :1020-1045. `unfold` builds the error from the whole `size` (TooLarge/Memory at :739-751). A refused or failed compact attempt returns that error: the early return at :768 and `held.budget.error.clone()` at :1034. The compact lower bound `firm` is used only for the refusal test and is never carried out. The field doc says "The derivation's size" (:450). cli/src/prove.rs:539 `too_large` prints the whole figures. .claude/rules/core-derivations.md:176 documents "gives up ... with the whole derivation's error", so this is deliberate, but it still misleads under `--compact always`. I ran the probe from audit/api-surface/gap/seq.txt (target/audit/release/linlog, capped scope). `--compact always --derivation-limit 12KiB` printed "its 339 inferences with 323764 characters of sequents are estimated at 2.5 MiB, over the limit of 12.0 KiB". `--derivation-limit 16KiB` wrote the compact tree. So the line names a derivation the caller did not ask for and gives no hint that 16 KiB would do. Narrower than the finding says: it only bites when `--compact` is `always`, or `auto` with a bound that a compact view cannot meet. In the default case the message is true of the whole derivation and its remedy works, so this is a UX/error-quality gap and not a wrong verdict. S18 (an error says what went wrong in terms of the caller's input) and C-INTERMEDIATE hold, but only at should-fix. The fix adds a `compact: Option<Least>` field to the error variants and a Display clause. It changes no pinned output, because the lock's examples are MLL proofs with no structural rule.

standing.title: Interactive recomputes the intuitionistic reading (O(n) over the whole forest) on every rules, apply, split_passes and derivation call: 2 000 one-formula queries on a 300 003-occurrence sequent take 2.1 s in intuitionistic mode against under 10 ms in classical mode
standing.evidence: `pub fn reading(&self) -> Option<Reading<'_>> { self.mode.intuitionistic.then(|| Reading::new(&self.forest).expect("checked when the proof was started")) }` (interactive.rs:438-442); `Reading::new` is one pass over every occurrence (`for o in forest.ids().rev()` and a second loop over the positions, reading.rs:197-240), and `Reading<'a>` keeps `forest: &'a Forest` beside `position: Box<[Position]>` (reading.rs:184-191), so the state cannot hold one. It is called afresh at every public step: `rules` (:520), `apply` (:546), `split_passes` (:758) and `derivation` (:922); only `from_parts` computes it once for the replay (:294). The rules file records it as a fact (core-derivations.md: "The reading is recomputed (`Interactive::reading`, O(n)) whenever intuitionistic mode needs positions, since `Reading` borrows the forest and the state owns it"). Measured, in the capped scope, with target/audit/release/linlog on a text sequent of 100 000 hypotheses `a1 -o a2, …, a100000 -o a100001 |- a1 -o a100001` (300 003 occurrences, scratchpad audit/ready-b/chain.txt) and a script of `rules 0 0` lines then `quit`, `linlog interact [-i] --jobs 1 -f chain.txt`, two runs each: classical, 1 query: wall 0.07 s; classical, 2 000 queries: wall 0.07 s; intuitionistic, 1 query: wall 0.07 s; intuitionistic, 2 000 queries: wall 2.18 s and 2.19 s (user 2.15 s), RSS 43 MB in all four. The whole difference is 2 000 readings of the forest, about 1.05 ms per `rules` query whose own work is a few rules on one formula; the command's `rules` handler (cli/src/interact.rs:183-195) does nothing else that depends on the mode. A client that lists the rules at each of the g positions of a goal before every redraw, which is what the step-32 web client does on each step, pays g readings of the whole sequent per step.
standing.fix: Keep the positions in the state: compute them once in `from_forest` (where `Reading::new(&forest)` already runs to validate the mode, :225) and store them beside the forest as an owned `Box<[Position]>` with the goal, and let `Reading<'a>`'s private `position` field be a `Cow<'a, [Position]>` (or give `Reading` a crate-private constructor from a forest, a borrowed position slice and the goal), so that `Interactive::reading` is O(1) and returns the same public `Option<Reading<'_>>`. Every field involved is private and every accessor keeps its signature, so no public item changes; this is also the owned positions-only value that R81 asks for and that `ProofStructure` can carry the same way for the essential nets of step 35 (R123). The behaviour lock does not change: no output, JSON form or snapshot is touched.

standing.title: Interactive::close_all drops the outcomes it has collected when a later goal errors or is stopped during its graft, while those goals' grafts stay in the state
standing.evidence: interactive.rs:866-867 reads `let outcome = self.close(goal, options, view, &mut stop)?; outcomes.push((goal, outcome));`. close grafts before it returns (`self.close_with(goal, proof, view, stop)?`, :826), and close_with answers Error::View when the graft is too large or `stop` fires while it is built (Derivation::of_goal polls it). standing.title: `Firm`, the compact view's lower bound that decides whether an `Auto` attempt is made, is pinned by no test
standing.evidence: core-derivations.md:170-174 states the property ("what a compact view holds at least (`size::Firm` …); an attempt is refused at once when that is over the bound"), and `unfold` acts on it (derivation.rs:768-769 `firm.bytes > most || firm.inferences > Derivation::MOST` refuses the compact view without trying). `grep -rn Firm core/src core/tests` finds `Firm` only in size.rs and at derivation.rs:737,768-769: no test compares `Firm` with a built compact view. standing.title: On a pool, every & premise copies the whole branch of ancestors into two new Vecs that the memory account does not count, so a nested & costs memory quadratic in its depth: a 35 KB sequent takes 823 MB under --memory-limit 64MiB
standing.evidence: `Engine::spawn` builds `branch: self.ancestors.iter().copied().chain([(&self.stack[..self.stack_len], &self.hashes[..self.stack_len])]).collect()` (parallel.rs:318-325), and `Spawn::worker` clones it again: `worker.ancestors = self.branch.clone();` (:211). `with_parallel` spawns with `self.spawn(self.or_depth)` (:485). It does not raise or_depth, so `cubes()` (or_depth < LEVELS) holds at every `&` of a branch that has met no choice. Each nested `&` therefore holds a Vec of k entries of two fat slices (32 bytes each) in its Spawn and another in its live right-hand worker, which is about 32·k² bytes over k nested levels. An entry is pushed even when the spawner's stack is empty. Neither Vec is charged to the account, although Options::memory_limit's doc (search/mod.rs:975-988) says the buffers every level of recursion takes are counted and lists only the forest, the returned proof and the net engine's structures as uncounted. The rules file says 'Nothing is copied' (.claude/rules/core-parallel.md:146). Input: `|- a * 1, ~a & (~a & ( … & ~a))` with n nested `&` (gen2.py in scratchpad/audit/input; the auto engine picks focus, MALL). Each run in the capped scope with /run/current-system/sw/bin/time -f '%e s %M KB': n=5000 `prove --jobs 1 -q --timeout 30s --recursion-limit 5010 --memory-limit 64MiB` → provable, 0.02 s, 23 612 KB; the same with `--jobs 2` → provable, 0.31 s, 823 100 KB. At the default recursion limit, `prove --jobs 2 -q --memory-limit 16MiB` on the same file → unknown (recursion limit 2048), 152 380 KB, against 13 884 KB with --jobs 1. The growth is quadratic (pure & tower `|- a, ~a & (…)`, --engine focus --jobs 2): n=1000 42 MB, 3000 (limit 3100) 306 MB, 5000 823 MB, 8000 2.08 GB, 10000 (limit 10100) 3.24 GB with --memory-limit 64MiB and with --no-check. The ratio 8000/5000 is 2.53 against (8/5)² = 2.56. The command accepts any u32 recursion limit, so the allocation has no bound a caller sets apart from the recursion limit, and at that limit it is quadratic. A side effect: `Engine::above` (focus/mod.rs:1166) and `Flags::raised` (search/parallel.rs:352-361) walk this chain on every call, which makes the time quadratic in the same depth.
standing.fix: Make the branch a persistent linked list instead of a copied Vec. A `Branch { keys, hashes, above: usize, parent: Option<&Branch> }` node lives in the Spawn, pointing to the spawner's own chain, and `worker.ancestors` becomes an `Option<&Branch>`. A spawn whose stack is empty reuses its parent's pointer, so a spawn is O(1), `above` reads the cached sum, and `repeated` walks the same entries as today. The alternative is to charge the Vecs to `problem.account` and give up with Reason::MemoryLimit. Correct the rules file's 'Nothing is copied' either way. No change to the behaviour lock: the counters on one thread are untouched, and on a pool only memory and time change.

Reproduced in the capped scope with target/audit/release/linlog on `|- a * 1, ~a & (~a & (… ))` (gen.py in my scratch dir), `prove -q --timeout 30s --recursion-limit n+10 --memory-limit 64MiB`, measured with GNU time %M: n=1000 jobs=1 7 940 KB, jobs=2 42 548 KB; n=2000 10 500 KB vs 142 132 KB; n=4000 18 436 KB vs 533 556 KB, all `provable (MALL, classical, focus engine)`. standing.title: A closed standard output turns a decided verdict into exit 2: `prove … | head -1` prints the verdict line and exits with status 2, and `check`, `seq`, the batch and `interact` do the same
standing.evidence: Rust ignores SIGPIPE, so a write to a closed pipe returns an EPIPE error. Every write site passes it up with `?`: `out.finish()?` (prove.rs:1047, 1111, 1257), `show.open`/`show.close` (prove.rs:328, 364), `io::write` (io.rs:187-197), the batch's `writeln!(stdout, …).context("cannot write to standard output")?` (batch.rs:969-971) and `writeln!(stdout, "{text}")?` in interact (interact.rs:143). `main` then maps every Err to `ERROR` (lib.rs:306-314: `Err(e) => { eprintln!("error: {e:#}"); ExitCode::from(ERROR) }`). This discards the status that prove.rs:1039-1043 had already computed before it wrote anything. Run in the capped scope with `set -o pipefail`, where L is a tensor of 200 atoms: `linlog prove --jobs 1 'L |- L' | head -1` printed `provable (MLL, classical, net engine)`, then `error: cannot write to standard output: Broken pipe (os error 32)`, and `status 2`. The same command into /dev/null gives status 0. When the whole output fits in the pipe, `L |- B | head -1` gives status 1, so the status depends on how large the output is. With standard output a pipe whose read end is already closed (a python runner, scratchpad closed.py), these all give `exit 2 … Broken pipe`: `prove 'A |- A'`, `prove 'A |- B'` (unprovable), `prove --format json`, `prove -q`, `check p.json` and `seq fragment`. A batch of 3000 lines (`prove --input-format lines --file many.txt | head -1`) gives status 2. `interact 'A |- A'` fed `goals` and then `save FILE` gives `exit 2 error: Broken pipe (os error 32)` with no context, and the session file is never written. These statements are false for these runs: README.md:410 ('The exit status tells scripts the verdict: 0 provable, 1 unprovable, 3 unknown … 2 an error') and README.md:419-420 ('keeps the verdict, with its exit status'). Neither the README nor cli.md says that a closed pipe gives 2. No test covers it: the test harnesses only tolerate BrokenPipe on the child's stdin (cli.rs:24-26, lock.rs:358-360, readme.rs:206-210). Step 17 §1.1 recorded this item and it still holds.
standing.fix: Decide once, in one place, what happens when standard output is closed. Proposal: have `io` mark a write error on standard output as `StdoutClosed`. One option is a wrapper type. The other is to check `e.chain()` for an `io::Error` of kind `BrokenPipe` from the stdout sink of `Output`/`io::write`. On that error, `prove` and `check` return the status they already decided, silently. The batch stops consuming results and returns the worst status so far. `interact` ends the session as it does at the end of input. `main` keeps exit 2 only for other errors. The other option is to restore SIGPIPE's default disposition at the start of `main`, which gives the shell's conventional 141 instead of 2. That is simpler, but it still loses the verdict, and README must then document 141. Add one CLI test that runs `prove` with stdout closed and asserts the verdict's status. Add one README sentence on the closed pipe. The behaviour lock does not change: no lock or README example runs with a closed stdout.

verdicts.evidence: Read cli/src/lib.rs:304-314 (`Err(e) => { eprintln!("error: {e:#}"); ExitCode::from(ERROR) }`), prove.rs:1039-1047 (status computed, then `out.finish()?`), io.rs:186-197, batch.rs:969-971, interact.rs:143 (`writeln!(stdout, "{text}")?` with no context). Ran in the capped scope with `set -o pipefail`: `linlog prove --jobs 1 --file L200.txt | head -1` printed `provable (MLL, classical, net engine)`, then `error: cannot write to standard output: Broken pipe (os error 32)`, status 2; the same into /dev/null status 0. With the pipe's read end closed (python runner): `prove 'A |- A'`, `prove 'A |- B'`, `prove -q 'A |- A'` all `exit 2 error: cannot write to standard output: Broken pipe`; `interact 'A |- A'` fed `goals` then `save FILE` gave `exit 2 error: Broken pipe (os error 32)` and no session file. The behaviour is as claimed and the status depends on the output's size. I give should-fix rather than must-fix: README:410 says '2 an error' and a failed write is an error, so no stated claim is false and no verdict is misread as another verdict; the concrete costs are S18's (interact's error lacks any context) and a status that varies with how much fits in the pipe. The fix the finding proposes is proportionate and does not touch the lock.

Read cli/src/lib.rs:306-314 (main maps every Err to ERROR) and cli/src/io.rs:187-197 (writeln! with context 'cannot write to standard output'). Ran in the capped scope with a 200-atom tensor sequent (scratchpad big.txt): `linlog prove --jobs 1 --file big.txt | head -1` printed the verdict line, then `error: cannot write to standard output: Broken pipe (os error 32)`, status 2; the same into /dev/null gave 0. A `seq print --format svg | head -c 100` also gave 2 with the same message. Holds as stated. No hit for SIGPIPE/BrokenPipe handling anywhere in cli/src. plan/28-audit-and-refactor.md:526 already lists 'a closed pipe keeps the verdict' as a stage-3 deliverable and plan/reports/17-assessment.md:107 recorded it, so it is a known, still-open item. Severity: the verdict was written before the pipe closed and exit 2 on a failed write is a defensible convention, so I rate it should-fix (a missing/false-by-omission README statement at README.md:410 plus lost status), not must-fix. The fix does not touch the behaviour lock.

standing.title: A large --timeout panics the command: the deadline adds the duration to an Instant unchecked
standing.evidence: `let end = start + limit;`. `parse_duration` (argument_parsing.rs:1224-1239) accepts any duration up to `Duration::MAX`. Run in the capped scope: `linlog prove --jobs 1 --timeout 18000000000000000000 '|- A, ~A'` and `--timeout 5000000000000000h` both give `panicked at cli/src/limit.rs:43:19: overflow when adding duration to instant`, status 101. `printf 'close\n' | linlog interact --jobs 1 --timeout 18000000000000000000 '|- A, ~A'` panics on the `close` thread, which loses an unsaved session. The same unchecked addition is at cli/src/batch.rs:711 (`Instant::now() + t + CHILD_GRACE`, the `--isolate` child's kill time).
standing.fix: Use `start.checked_add(limit)` at both places and treat `None` as no limit. Alternatively, refuse durations above a stated cap in `parse_duration` with a clap error. No change to the behaviour lock: only inputs that panic today change.

also.evidence:
`Deadline::start` computes `let end = start + limit;` with no check, and `parse_time` accepts any duration that fits a `Duration`.
`linlog prove --timeout 10000000000000000000 'A |- A'` gives `thread 'main' panicked at cli/src/limit.rs:43:19: overflow when adding duration to instant`.
`linlog prove --batch-timeout 10000000000000000000 --input-format lines -` panics at the same place.

Ran in the capped scope: `linlog prove --jobs 1 --timeout 18000000000000000000 '|- A, ~A'` → `thread 'main' panicked at cli/src/limit.rs:43:19: overflow when adding duration to instant`, status 101. batch.rs:707-711 computes `Instant::now() + t + CHILD_GRACE` the same way. standing.title: `--jobs 2` with `--pool-after` (and the default on a two-thread machine) runs three searching threads
standing.evidence:
`let pool = threads.jobs.saturating_sub(1).max(2);` puts a pool of two beside the single thread when jobs is 2. `--jobs` help (argument_parsing.rs:183-195) says "How many threads the search may use". Measured on the 2^42-split sequent of cli/tests/cli.rs::timeout with `-a --timeout 2s`:
- `--jobs 2 --pool-after 50ms`: real 2.003 s, user 5.890 s (three threads)
- `--jobs 2`: user 3.994 s
- `--deterministic`: user 1.996 s
The harness copy (bench/src/run.rs:740) does the same, so its rows labelled `jobs` 2 ran three threads.
standing.fix: When `jobs <= 2`, skip the race: run `jobs` threads from the start, or one thread then a pool of `jobs - 1` only when that is at least 2. Otherwise use a pool of `jobs - 1`. Fix both copies, or better the one shared function (see the race finding). The behaviour lock is unchanged: lock calls are `--deterministic` or decide before the pool starts.

also.evidence: The `--jobs` help (argument_parsing.rs:183) says 'How many threads the search may use'. `alone_first` keeps the single thread and starts `let pool = threads.jobs.saturating_sub(1).max(2);` beside it. So `--jobs 2 --pool-after 1s` searches on 1 + 2 threads. `threads()` (argument_parsing.rs:428-447) keeps `alone` for any `jobs > 1` when `--pool-after` is nonzero. The same holds for interact's `--jobs` ('How many threads a `close` may use; see prove --jobs', argument_parsing.rs:363). This is one of the leftovers listed in plan/28-audit-and-refactor.md (steps 21 and 24) and still holds.
also.fix: With `alone` set, make the pool `jobs − 1`, and when that would be one, run the pool alone with no single thread beside it (or refuse `--pool-after` for `--jobs 2`). Or change the help to say what is counted. Behaviour lock: only runs with `--jobs 2 --pool-after` change, in their thread count; their verdicts do not.

verdicts.evidence: prove.rs:71 `let pool = threads.jobs.saturating_sub(1).max(2);` beside the single thread of 77-91, which is not stopped when the pool starts (102-103), so `jobs == 2` with a nonzero `alone` runs 1 + 2 threads; `threads()` (argument_parsing.rs:428-447) keeps `alone` for any `jobs > 1` with `--pool-after`, and by default (`None` arm) on a two-thread machine. The `--jobs` help (argument_parsing.rs:183) says `How many threads the search may use`, and `--pool-after`'s long help (200-202) says `a pool of the other threads`, so both overstate by one for N=2. Measured in the capped scope on the `cli.rs::timeout` sequent with `-a --timeout 2s`: `--jobs 2 --pool-after 50ms` real 2.00 s user 5.88 s; `--jobs 2` user 3.98 s; `--deterministic` user 1.99 s: three threads. bench/src/run.rs:740 has the same line. S11 must-fix (the help is false for 2) and S1 hold.

Read cli/src/prove.rs:55-123 and cli/src/argument_parsing.rs:183-208, 420-448. `threads()` keeps `alone` whenever jobs > 1 and the time is nonzero. `alone_first` spawns the single thread, then after `alone` runs `search(.. .jobs(pool))` with `pool = threads.jobs.saturating_sub(1).max(2)`. With jobs = 2 that is 1 + 2 = 3 searching threads, while `--jobs` is documented as 'How many threads the search may use'. For jobs >= 3 the total is exactly jobs, so only the jobs = 2 case overshoots. It is reached by `--jobs 2 --pool-after X` and by the default on a two-thread machine. bench/src/run.rs:735-740 has the same line and the same comment. I did not re-measure the user times; the code settles it. The harm is one extra thread, not unbounded, so I rate it should-fix rather than must-fix. The proposed fix leaves the behaviour lock unchanged.

standing.title: A PNG or PDF of a derivation holds the whole SVG in a String before any bound is compared: 80 MB peak under --memory-limit 34MiB
standing.evidence: For a binary format, `derivation` runs `let mut drawing = String::new(); if svg::write(&d, &styles.svg, &mut drawing, &mut halt).is_err()` (prove.rs:667-668), then `render(drawing, …)`, which only then compares `png::Options::memory` and `pixels`. cli/src/ordinary.rs:120-121 does the same, and so do the session's `show --png` and a batch of drawings, which go through `render`. `Show::within` (prove.rs:264-266) promises 'every derivation and the check behind it, and every render, within `memory` bytes', and the `--memory-limit` help says a render is 'estimated before it starts … and left out above the limit'. Run in the capped scope on `wide512.txt` (the wide sequent with k=512; derivation 2 559 inferences, estimated at 32.1 MiB). `linlog prove --jobs 1 --derivation-limit none --memory-limit 34MiB --format png --output w.png --file wide512.txt` peaked at maxrss 66 944 KiB. With `--style svg.ids=true` it peaked at 80 640 KiB. Both were then refused ('the image would have 7155131916 pixels'). The same drawing streamed with `--format svg --output w.svg` (57.8 MB, 71.6 MB with ids) peaked at 14.3 MB at most. Holding the SVG gains nothing: `Measure::estimate` charges at least `PNG.byte`/`PDF.byte` = 2 bytes per byte of SVG (export/mod.rs:190, 202), so any SVG longer than half the memory bound is certain to be refused.
standing.fix: Write the drawing into a String that fails once it passes the bound: `memory / 2`, or better a bound the library exports (for example `png::Options::max_svg_bytes()`, or a `Measure` that is fed incrementally as a `fmt::Write`). Answer the same `Rendered::Refused` line as now. The root's size is written in the head before any inference, so the pixel bound can be checked there as well. Output does not change below the bound. Above it the line could name the memory bound instead of the pixels, which would change the lock only if it pins such a refusal.

verdicts.evidence: Read cli/src/prove.rs:666-679: `let mut drawing = String::new(); if svg::write(&d, &styles.svg, &mut drawing, &mut halt).is_err() ... render(drawing, ...)`, and ordinary.rs:119-121 the same; render (prove.rs:819-852) hands the whole String to `png::from_svg`, whose `Measure::of` (export/mod.rs:283) is the first bound compared. `Show::within` (prove.rs:264-266) states 'every render, within `memory` bytes' and the `--memory-limit` help (argument_parsing.rs:170-173) 'estimated before it starts ... and left out above the limit'. Ran in the capped scope on a tensor of 400 atoms (text estimate under 34 MiB): `prove --jobs 1 --derivation-limit none --memory-limit 34MiB --format svg --output w.svg` streamed a 52 313 005-byte file at maxrss 14 276 KiB; the same with `--format png --output w.png` peaked at maxrss 60 428 KiB and was then refused ('the image would have 4673315556 pixels'). The process held a 52 MB drawing under a 34 MiB bound before any bound was compared, as the finding says; `PNG.byte = 2` (export/mod.rs:190) means any SVG over half the bound is certain to be refused, so holding it gains nothing.

Read cli/src/prove.rs:665-681: for a binary format `let mut drawing = String::new(); svg::write(&d, &styles.svg, &mut drawing, &mut halt)` with `d` still alive, then `drop(d)` and render(); the pixel/memory comparison happens only inside the render. export/mod.rs:190,202 confirm PNG/PDF charge byte: 2 plus base 32 MiB, so an SVG over memory/2 is certain to be refused, and Show::within (prove.rs:264-266) promises renders within memory. The overshoot is a constant factor (derivation plus SVG String, about 2.5x the bound in the finding's measurement) bounded by what the derivation admission allowed, not unbounded, so should-fix rather than must-fix. I did not re-run the wide512 measurement (the input file is not in the repo); the code path is as quoted. Fix is cheap (a limited fmt::Write) and does not change the lock.

standing.title: The formatter hook silently skips every file when the session's working directory is not the repository root, while CLAUDE.md says it runs on each file changed with Write or Edit

A session whose shell has done `cd core` (the Bash tool keeps its working directory) has a cwd with no flake.nix in it, so nothing gets formatted, and the same goes for a file outside the cwd's subtree. I traced it in the capped scope with `bash -x .claude/hooks/format.sh` and the payload {"tool_input":{"file_path":".../linlog/core/src/lib.rs"},"cwd":".../linlog/core"}: `+ cd /home/tux/Projects/own/linlog/core`, `+ '[' -f flake.nix ']'`, `+ exit 0`, so `nix fmt` never runs. Following that, a session expects the formatting done, finds out only when the treefmt check fails, and the hook fails silently by design.
standing.fix: Walk up from the cwd (or from the file) to the nearest directory holding flake.nix and use that as the root. That still keeps a worktree's own root, the reason the hook reads `cwd`. Then require the file to lie under that root. The behaviour lock does not change.

standing.title: Minimal logic under the call-by-value translation refutes valid sequents: the minimal `false` atom lacks the `!` every other CBV atom has
standing.evidence:
The arm `_ if minimal_false => make(0, Atom, None, None)` precedes the `CallByValue` arm whose atoms are `make(1, Atom, …)` (translate.rs:180), and the root loop (translate.rs:408-415) gives a CBV hypothesis no `!` of its own, because every CBV image is meant to carry one. A bare `false` on the left cannot be weakened, contracted or stand beside a promotion.
`linlog seq print --logic minimal --translation cbv 'false |- a -> a'` gives `false ⊢ !(!a ⊸ !a)`; `linlog prove --logic minimal --translation cbv -q 'false |- a -> a'` gives `not valid (…, two-sided engine): the image is unprovable: ~false occurs 1 more time than false …`, exit 1. Likewise `a, false |- a`, `false, false |- false`, `false |- false /\ false`, `false /\ a |- a` and `false \/ a |- true` (the last by an exhaustive search). `--translation cbn` and `01` answer `valid` on each, and `--logic intuitionistic --translation cbv` too (there false is `0`).
A differential test of 26 460 ordinary calls against truth tables and an independent G4ip prover found this the only wrong verdict (114 calls). Reproduced by the supervisor at 1d144ec6 (the library and command sources are unchanged since main).
standing.fix: Give the arm the CBV atom's shape (one `!` when the translation is `CallByValue`), or move the minimal-false case into each translation's match so that it is the atom case. The read-back takes its `!` count from the pattern and needs no change. Add `false |- a -> a` (valid in all three logics) to `decides_and_reads_back`; no case there has `false` standing positively in a hypothesis of a valid minimal sequent, and cli/tests/cli.rs pins only `a, a -> b |- b` for minimal/cbv.

standing.title: The pool overflows its stack under a raised --recursion-limit: a waiting thread runs a stolen job's whole recursion on top of its own

Generator: `n=2900; C(i) = 'b & ('*n + 'c%d' % i + ')'*n; '|- ' + ', '.join('?('+C(i)+')' for i in range(2)) + ', ~b'` (35 KB). `linlog prove -q -j 2 --affine --recursion-limit 3000 -f F` aborts (`has overflowed its stack`, exit 134); `--deterministic` gives unknown at the recursion limit, exit 3. At the default limit of 2048 no abort on two threads; more threads allow more nesting. The `unknown` message tells the user to raise the limit, and a batch without --isolate loses every answer.

standing.title: A `.p` file without --logic is read as LLTP, so an intuitionistically valid ILTP problem is answered unprovable
standing.evidence: `InputFormat::of` maps `.p` to LLTP unless --logic is given (argument_parsing.rs:614-621); both libraries write `fof(…)`, and TPTP's `&`, `|`, `~` parse as with, par and negation. `fof(c, conjecture, ~ (p & ~ p)).` (ILTP status Theorem): `linlog prove -q --file nc.p` gives `unprovable (ALL, classical, focus engine)`, exit 1; with `--logic intuitionistic`, `valid`. Files with `=>` or `<=>` fail to parse, which is safe. Documented, and the verdict line names the linear fragment.
standing.fix: Keep LLTP as the reading of `.p` (the harness and the LLTP batch rely on it), and say in the `unprovable` line or a note on standard error that the file was read as linear logic when its clauses use only `&`, `|` and `~`; or refuse the ambiguity. The area judges.

standing.title: No test compares the ordinary layer's translations with each other or with an oracle on generated sequents
standing.evidence: H1 makes call-by-value disagree with call-by-name and the 01 translation on `false |- a -> a` in minimal logic, and nothing in the suite notices: `decides_and_reads_back` lists cases by hand, and the generated-sequent tests of `search::reference` cover the linear engines, not the ordinary layer. A differential run of 26 460 ordinary calls (classical against truth tables, intuitionistic and minimal against an independent G4ip-style prover) found H1 and nothing else.
standing.fix: A test over generated ordinary sequents, as `search::reference` does for the engines: in each logic the translations agree with each other, and in classical logic with a truth table; the cases kept small enough for the suite's time.

refuted.title: The batch demands Send + 'static of its problems and closures and boxes a dyn Iterator + Send even on the sequential path, which a wasm wrapper holding JavaScript handles cannot meet
refuted.evidence: pub fn prove(problems: impl IntoIterator<Item = Problem, IntoIter: Send + 'static>, …) (batch.rs:163-166) and pub fn run<P, R>(…, work: impl Fn(P, &Search) -> R + Send + Sync + 'static) where P: Send + 'static, R: Send + 'static (:180-188) carry the bounds without any cfg; Inner::Here(Box<dyn Iterator<Item = R> + Send>) (:221) is the path taken without the feature and with one worker.
