refuted.fix: Bounds under cfg(feature = "parallel") only (a trait alias or two signatures selected by cfg), Inner::Here without Send; a compile test in the no-default-features build. No change of the behaviour lock.

verdicts.evidence: The bounds are as quoted (core/src/search/batch.rs:162-188, Inner::Here `Box<dyn Iterator<Item = R> + Send>` at :221). The finding still fails on three points. (1) S12 is not broken: a Send bound reads no clock and spawns no thread, the library builds for wasm with it, and a wrapper can collect its problems into a Vec<Problem> (Send) before calling. (2) R48 (requirements.md:437-442) lists the batch step (done) and the web client, not 28. The finding itself says 'Relaxing later is compatible', and relaxing a bound or adding a non-Send sequential entry after 0.1.0 is additive, so per the rubric this is a later step's deliverable that today's code need not prepare for. (3) The proposed fix, bounds 'under cfg(feature = "parallel") only', would make `parallel` a non-additive feature. Through cargo's feature unification, any crate in the graph that enables `parallel` would break another crate's non-Send call, so the fix costs more than the defect. The alternative (a separate sequential entry) is additive and can wait for its caller.

Facts are right (batch.rs:163-166, 180-188 carry Send + 'static unconditionally; Inner::Here is Box<dyn Iterator + Send>, :221). But: (1) the register item R48 (requirements.md:437-443) lists the web client as its step, and nothing in plan/32-web.md or plan/notes/research/32-web.md mentions the batch at all (grep), so 'the wasm client is the batch's second caller' is unsupported; (2) relaxing generic bounds later is source-compatible, so S16 (no breaking change after 0.1.0) does not require preparing now; (3) the proposed fix, bounds under cfg(feature = "parallel"), makes the public signature depend on a non-additive feature that cargo unifies across the dependency graph, so a wasm crate would silently get Send bounds back when anything enables parallel; a separate non-Send sequential entry is the sound shape and is a later step's deliverable. Problem is plain owned data, so a wasm wrapper can materialise a Vec<Problem> today.

refuted.title: The forest has one meaning for roots, ids and sequent, and every reader assumes the forest is exactly the conclusion
refuted.evidence: `Forest` is built only from a whole `Sequent` (`new`, `within`, `from_owned`, `TryFrom`, occurrences/mod.rs:202-223, 387-397) and `roots()` (:264) is the sequent's roots; nothing tells a conclusion from a further tree. Readers that take the whole forest for the conclusion: `is_roots` (search/mod.rs:390-403, sets `task.roots`), `few_equal_literals` over `forest.literals` (:633-641), the net engine's `counts_admit` over `forest.ids()` and `forest.roots().len()` (search/net.rs:136-160) and its `expect("a complete linking … is a proof net")` (:121-124), `Reading::new` choosing the goal among `forest.roots()` (occurrences/reading.rs:221-235), `Classes::new` over `forest.ids()` (search/focus/classes.rs:31-45), `ProofStructure::new` taking the fragment of `forest.sequent()` (nets/mod.rs:203). Step 34 appends `A`, `A⊥` per cut after the roots (research/34-cut.md §2); with that, a goal equal to the conclusion is `is_roots`, the net engine takes the whole forest and its `expect` panics (impact-boxes.md §5), and `Reading::new` fails with `SeveralGoals` on the cut roots. None of this breaks a signature, but what the accessors denote is a contract the Rocq checker (31) and the web client (32) build on before 34.
refuted.fix: State the contract on `Forest` now: `roots()` is the conclusion in written order, `sequent()` the conclusion whose arena may hold terms the roots do not reach, `ids()`/`len()`/`all_literals()` everything the forest holds, which later constructors may extend past the roots; reserve an empty `cut_pairs()` accessor; make `is_roots` mean "the goal is every tree of the forest" (compare with `len()` of the trees, not only the roots) and have `Reading::new` and the net engine read the conclusion through one accessor. No behaviour or output changes today: the behaviour lock is unchanged.

verdicts.evidence: The citations are accurate: is_roots (search/mod.rs:389-403), few_equal_literals (:633-641), counts_admit using `forest.roots().len()` (search/net.rs:136-160), the `expect` (:121-124) and Reading::new over `forest.roots()` (occurrences/reading.rs:221-235). The defect, though, is step 34's own deliverable, which today's code need not prepare for. R57's 'Met when' (separate cut-root accessors, a test that adds a cut, the occurrence limit on additions) and R98/R99 (Steps: 34 session 1 only) all name step 34's work. The finding concedes that no signature breaks. Today `roots()` is already documented as 'the occurrence of each root formula, in the order the sequent lists them' (occurrences/mod.rs:262-264), which is the conclusion, and `len()`/`ids()` are 'every occurrence'. Cut roots can be added later through a new constructor and a new accessor without breaking either. is_roots, few_equal_literals and counts_admit are crate-private and get rewritten once, by step 34, so there is no second rewrite. Reserving an empty `cut_pairs()` accessor now would add API for a feature that does not exist yet. The rubric excludes a later step's deliverable that today's code need not prepare (rubric, Severities, last paragraph).

Read core/src/occurrences/mod.rs:155-270 and R57/R98/R99/R119 in plan/notes/requirements.md. Forest::roots() already documents itself as 'the occurrence of each root formula, in the order the sequent lists them' (mod.rs:260-263), and Forest is built only from a whole Sequent. The finding itself says 'None of this breaks a signature'. Adding cut roots later is additive: Forest has private fields, and new constructors and accessors do not break Forest::new. The register's Met-when for R57, R98 and R99 is step 34's deliverable (separate cut-root accessors, restricted is_roots, Reading::new on cut pairs). The proposed empty cut_pairs() accessor and the reworked is_roots/Reading::new would be speculative code for an undesigned feature, so today's code need not prepare for them (rubric: a later step's own deliverable is no finding; a place is missing only if S16 needs a breaking change, and none is shown). The only residual is one sentence in core-forest.md or core-proofs.md recording the Rust decision that R57 asks of step 28, which is a documentation line and not a should-fix defect.

refuted.title: The interactive state recomputes the whole reading on every rules() and apply() call
refuted.evidence: `fn reading(&self) -> Option<Reading<'_>> { self.mode.intuitionistic.then(|| Reading::new(&self.forest).expect(…)) }` (proofs/interactive.rs:438-442); `rules` calls it (:520) and `apply` calls it (:546); `Reading::new` is one pass over `forest.len()` occurrences with a `Box<[Position]>` allocated (occurrences/reading.rs:197-235), so every click of an intuitionistic session costs the size of the whole forest, which the web client of step 32 multiplies by the number of clicks on a state of thousands of occurrences. The state owns the forest and `Reading` borrows it, which is why it is not stored.
refuted.fix: Keep the positions and the goal in the state (an owned `Box<[Position]>` plus `OccId`, computed once in `from_forest`) and build the borrowing `Reading` view from them in O(1) (a crate-private constructor from parts), so a click costs the goal's size. Same positions, same answers: the behaviour lock is unchanged.

verdicts.evidence: The code is as quoted: Interactive::reading (core/src/proofs/interactive.rs:438-442) calls Reading::new on every call, from rules (:520), apply (:546), split_passes (:758) and derivation (:922). Reading::new (occurrences/reading.rs:197-240) is two linear passes over forest.len() bytes plus a Box<[Position]>. Two things refute the finding as stated. (1) A1 says a claim of slowness rests on a count, profile or time and never on reading alone, and none is given. At a few ns per occurrence, a state of 10 000 occurrences costs tens of microseconds per click. (2) R93 (requirements.md:853-859) lists steps 32 and 22, not 28, and its Met when (reading held in the state, a filtering rules, a benchmark of 10 000-occurrence states) is a web-client deliverable. Storing the positions is internal: Reading's public API and reading()'s signature stay, so step 32 can make the change without any break. The place is not missing, so S16 does not apply. core-derivations.md already documents the recomputation as a deliberate choice.

The code is as described: reading() (interactive.rs:438-442) calls Reading::new(&self.forest), one pass over forest.len() with a Vec<u8> and a boxed position slice (occurrences/reading.rs:197-235), from rules() (:520), apply() (:546), split_passes (:758) and derivation (:922). But A1 says a claim of slowness rests on a count, a profile or a time, never on reading alone, and the finding gives none. The cost is linear in the forest per user click, which is small beside work these calls already do (apply copies the goal with to_vec, builds Multisets). Step 17's assessment item 10 flagged it only as an ownership question. Unmeasured micro-optimisation is taste under A1; I did not measure it either.

refuted.title: The statistics of two searches are merged by hand beside Statistics::add
refuted.evidence: `Statistics::add` (search/mod.rs:1494-1503) leaves out the memo counters ("they describe a table, not a run"). Both of its two-search callers then add them back by hand, each its own way. `turns` (schedule.rs:72-74) does `statistics.add(&run); statistics.memo_hits += run.memo_hits; statistics.memo_entries = statistics.memo_entries.max(run.memo_entries)`. `merged` (schedule.rs:552-555) does `add`, then `memo_hits +=` and `memo_entries +=`. The rule for each lives in the doc of `Statistics::memo_entries` (1473-1476) and in these two bodies. Step 17 (item 3) noted the three counting rules. They are now documented, but they are still written out where they are used.
refuted.fix: Add one method that states the rule, e.g. `Statistics::add_search(&mut self, other, entries: Entries::{Sum, Most})`, and call it from both places. It does the same arithmetic, so the reported counters stay identical. No change to the behaviour lock.

verdicts.evidence: Read schedule.rs:72-74 and 552-555 and `Statistics::add` (search/mod.rs:1494-1503). The two bodies differ by design: `turns` takes the most entries of one turn (`max`), `merged` the two memos together (`+=`), exactly as the field's doc (mod.rs:1473-1476) states, and the pool's third caller (`Collected::take`, focus/parallel.rs:243; net.rs:977) wants neither, since it reads the memo off the shared table. The only line written twice is `statistics.memo_hits += ..memo_hits`. A `add_search(other, Entries::{Sum, Most})` would be a method of the same length as the four lines it replaces, with an enum to name the two rules that are already named at the field. The criteria do not decide this: it is a preference between two equally clear forms, so taste under the rubric, not A6's 'copied walk, table, race or verdict line'.

Read search/mod.rs:1465-1503 and schedule.rs:60-75 and 552-555. The two callers differ on purpose: `turns` runs sequentially and takes the larger `memo_entries` of one turn, while `merged` runs two searches together and adds the two memos' entries. The rule for each is documented on `Statistics::memo_entries` (mod.rs:1473-1476). The proposed `add_search(.., Entries::{Sum,Most})` would move one `+=` and one `max` line behind an enum argument and would not remove any duplicated logic. The defect costs less than the fix, and I count it as taste.

refuted.title: The Typst layout's spacing fields are strings of Typst code written verbatim, unchecked, unlike svg::Style's typed lengths
refuted.evidence: `pub premise_gap: String`, `label_gap`, `band`, `stroke` (typst.rs:162-175) are spliced in as `let gap = ({}).to-absolute()` and `let stroke = {}` (typst.rs:505-510). Probes: `--style 'typst.premise_gap="1.5"' --style typst.layout=linlog` writes `let gap = (1.5).to-absolute()` (a float, not a length: Typst rejects it at compile time, linlog exits 0); `--style 'typst.stroke="0.05em) panic(1"'` writes `let stroke = 0.05em) panic(1` into the document. svg::Style's spacing fields are `u32` thousandths of an em (svg/mod.rs:82-91).
refuted.fix: Type the four fields as lengths, e.g. `u32` thousandths of an em as svg::Style does, written with the SVG's `decimal` as `1.5em` etc. (defaults 1500, 200, 800, 50 give today's text byte for byte, so no snapshot changes), or a `Length { value, unit }` validated at construction. The JSON and `--style typst.premise_gap=…` value type changes (strings to numbers): help text (cli/src/argument_parsing.rs:896-897) and README lines 618-628 change in the same commit; the behaviour lock is untouched.

verdicts.evidence: Read core/src/export/typst.rs:162-176 (the four `String` fields, each documented 'a Typst length') and typst.rs:505-510 where they are spliced as `let gap = ({}).to-absolute()` and `let stroke = {}`. The neighbouring fields `import` (typst.rs:157) and `page` (typst.rs:159) are arbitrary Typst code written verbatim by design, and .claude/rules/core-export.md says so of the spacing fields explicitly ('Typst lengths written verbatim, as `import` and `page` are; their defaults are curryst's'). The 'injection' probe injects Typst into the user's own Typst document, which `page` already allows, so it shows no new capability. The comparison with svg::Style's `u32` thousandths of an em does not carry: SVG computes its own layout and needs numbers; Typst measures with `to-absolute()` and accepts any length or expression (`0.5em + 1pt`, `2pt`), which the proposed `u32` em-only type would forbid. A4/C-CUSTOM-TYPE do not decide between a typed em-length and a string of target code when the sibling fields are target code: both idioms are allowed, and the fix costs a JSON type change plus a loss of units for no measured benefit. Taste. The one defensible residue (an unparseable value compiles to a bad document at exit 0) is api-wire-21's C-VALIDATE point, judged there.

Code and quote hold: core/src/export/typst.rs:162-175 are Strings spliced at :505-510. But it is a recorded decision: .claude/rules/core-export.md:157-159 says the spacing fields are 'Typst lengths written verbatim, as `import` and `page` are'. Those two (typst.rs:156,158) are Typst code and cannot be typed either; `stroke` is a full Typst stroke expression (colour, dash, `0.5pt + red`), and lengths may be `1em + 2pt`, so the proposed u32 thousandths of em would remove expressivity SVG never had. Passing a wrong string yields the user's own broken Typst, reported by `typst compile`, not a silently wrong verdict, so C-VALIDATE's must-fix test (invalid argument gives a wrong answer silently) is not met. A validated Length type would be an optional enhancement (taste), not a defect.

The premise is false. prove_until's own example (core/src/search/mod.rs:171-184) does use Instant, but it is not 'the one' example. The crate docs (core/src/lib.rs:47-63) show prove_until with a work-counting stop (`let mut budget = 1000; ... budget -= 1; budget == 0`) and say 'since this crate has no clock'. The Instant example is true for native callers, and the library reads no clock, so neither S12 nor S11 is broken. lib.rs:89 already says `parallel` is 'never for WebAssembly'. The feature table for a wasm client is R49's Met when (requirements.md:446-450, step 32), and the wasm check and the stop type are R41 and R243 (steps 30, 32), as the finding itself concedes. taste.title: A zone over `Bag::MOST` is a verdict, not a refusal
taste.note: `within` caps `room` at `Bag::MOST` (2³² − 2), so a correct proof whose zone is larger (a goal of billions of roots and a proof of billions of nodes, well over 100 GB) would be `Problem::Surplus`, 'invalid', rather than a refusal. Out of reach by orders of magnitude; the rules file says 'never more than Bag::MOST' and could say in one sentence that it is a verdict there by design.

taste.title: `from_proof` reads the `Ax` nodes through a wildcard
taste.note: `filter_map(|n| match *n { Node::Ax(x, y) => Some((x, y)), _ => None })` is R254's place for step 34: a `Cut` variant would be silently ignored and the Ax links could pass `is_correct` with Mix as a net of another sequent. No wrong net arises today; an explicit match with a refusing arm per unread kind costs one `match` now.

taste.title: The abbreviation of error reports is pinned by the command's lock only
taste.note: The mutants at :380, :424, :562 and :651 (`Described::abbreviated` dropping its `limit`, the `Budget` cut) survive the library's tests; whether `--abbreviate` is in `cli/tests/lock` decides if anything pins it. A unit test of `Described::abbreviated(Some(n))` on the report of `error_message` would pin the library's own promise.

taste.title: `InfId` counts of the read-back and the session are argued by appeal to memory, not at a bound
taste.note: `push` says the read-back's inferences are 'far below u32::MAX for any proof a search returns within its memory bound' and the session's `base + i` (interactive.rs:565) says nothing; both are true in practice (a derivation is bounded by `Derivation::MOST` and the view's limit; a session grows by hand). Neither is a checker's integer, so no S3 finding, but a saturating `count` as derivation.rs:803 has would make both self-evident.

taste.title: `merged` lets the first search's refutation win over the second's proof
taste.note: `merged` matches `(Ok(root), _)` first, so if the two searches of the default bias ever disagreed, a forward `Ok(None)` would be answered `Unprovable` with the backward search's proof discarded; the `debug_assert!` that they agree is gone in release builds. The identity argument of core-focus.md says they cannot disagree, so this is not a finding; but a checked proof is the stronger evidence, and matching `Ok(Some(_))` of either before `Ok(None)` costs nothing and makes the merge safe against a future engine bug.

taste.title: The sums of `Tally` and `Split` carry no argument for their `i32` width at the declaration
taste.note: `Counts::lo`/`hi` say why they fit an `i32` (a forest that gets counts has fewer than 2³¹ occurrences); `Tally::lo`/`hi` and `Split::lo`/`hi`/`below`/`above` sum rows over the members of a zone and say nothing. They fit because the members of a stable sequent are distinct occurrences with disjoint subtrees (a repeat in `Γ` comes only from a copy out of `Θ`, whose atoms have no row), except for the repeats a caller puts in a `prove_goal` goal itself, which the occurrence limit does not bound. A sentence at the declaration, or a bound on the goal's length, would make S3's argument visible; reaching the limit needs a goal of 2³¹ entries.

taste.title: Two mutants the baseline lists as surviving were caught by a test and timed out on another

taste.title: The pair's `Unknown` reason is the backward search's (register R138)

taste.title: The counts are built for every affine Horn call although no counts refutation applies there

taste.note: R87 asks that each `Row` carry its evidence; today the rustdoc table on `Engine` holds it, which core-search.md names as the place. A `note: &'static str` per row or a test that the table and DISPATCH list the same rows would make the link checkable.

taste.title: The ids of an SVG net are documented as occurrences
taste.note: "the id `o<n>` for occurrence `n`": once the vertex decision of R77 is made, the doc should say vertex (the occurrence in MLL) and reserve prefixes for boxes, doors, jumps and cut links, so that step 32's client binds to a grammar step 33 keeps.

taste.title: Uneven selection of crate-root re-exports
taste.note: The root re-exports generic names that lose their module there (Scratch, the net test's buffer; Size; Side; Compact beside ViewOptions; Labels, OpenGoal, WriteError of the exports, while Form and RenderError stay under export) and leaves out the partners of what it re-exports (UnknownRule for Rule::from_str, Described for CheckError::describe, DescribedShape, Dyadic, check::Problem, search::Pool and engine_for beside prove_goal, batch::Cores). A rule for what the root carries would settle it.

taste.title: Who owns the forest
taste.note: Proof::new and ProofStructure::new take an owned Forest, so the engines clone it into every proof and net (search/mod.rs:450, search/net.rs:227, nets/sequentialize.rs:37, nets/mod.rs:258, interactive.rs:967) and Interactive::new clones the sequent; a shared forest (Arc) would avoid it. No measurement was taken, so this is no A1 finding.

taste.title: Writers take `&mut impl fmt::Write`
taste.note: C-RW-VALUE prefers the writer by value; with fmt::Write implemented for &mut W that would also accept the String the String twins use. Both idioms work.

taste.title: `ordinary` writes while `derivation` returns a String in every export module
taste.note: latex, typst, svg and rocq each have `derivation(&d, &o) -> String`, `write(…)` and `ordinary(…)` which writes; `write_ordinary` would say what it does (the usability baseline's single-task friction).

taste.title: Engine::parallel reads as a verb
taste.note: A bool query named `parallel()`; `runs_on_pool()` or `is_parallel()` would read as a question.

taste.title: unwrap in the batch module's example
taste.note: C-QUESTION-MARK: the doc example uses `text.parse().unwrap()` and `answer.outcome.unwrap()`; the other examples use `?`.

taste.title: Eight types called Options
taste.note: search, batch, latex, typst, png, pdf, rocq and ordinary each have an Options; module-qualified names are idiomatic, but batch.rs already imports `Options as Search` to tell its own from the search's, and the usability readers named the collision.

taste.title: Tuples returned by the families
taste.note: `counter -> (Sequent, u32)` and `qbf -> (Sequent, bool)`; Instance already names these fields.

taste.title: Interactive recomputes the reading per call
taste.note: rules, apply and split_passes each run Reading::new (O(forest)); R93 asks it stored. Unmeasured here, so left to the efficiency lens.

taste.title: Sequent JSON key names
taste.note: `ids` holds the roots' term indices, while every other form uses ids for occurrence ids, and `var_dict` holds atom names. AIP-140 would rename them to `roots` and `atoms`. R251 keeps V, D and var_dict on the wire so that stored files do not change. If the version key lands, the rename could ride on it; otherwise leave it.

taste.title: The Proof JSON key `proof` holds the nodes
taste.note: The Rust names them `nodes`. A key `proof` inside a proof object, flattened into the outcome, reads oddly; `nodes` would say what it holds. It is a format break, so only worth doing with the version key.

taste.title: `once` names a boolean by an adverb
taste.note: In `state_equation`, `once` means 'some clause used once weighs something too'. A noun such as `once_clauses_weighted` would say what it holds. R70 settles the meaning of `weights` and `once` before 0.1.0.

taste.title: `atom` means an index in Rust and a name in JSON
taste.note: In Refutation::Unbalanced, the Rust field `atom` is the Atom index and `name` the name; the JSON writes the name under `atom`. Both are documented, but the same word means different things across the two.

taste.title: check takes the mode from flags while the outcome it reads carries one
taste.note: `prove --affine --format json | linlog check` reports `invalid proof … the mode forbids the rule`, exit 1. This is documented in `check --help` ('pass the flags the proof was found with'). R7, a mode key on the proof form, is step 31's additive key, so it is not counted as a finding.

taste.title: check's JSON sorts its keys
taste.note: `serde_json::json!` without preserve_order writes `affine, intuitionistic, mix` and `error, mode, valid`, unlike the insertion order of every library form. This is harmless to parsers but not byte-stable against the rest.

taste.title: An error message names a Rust function
taste.note: TooManyOccurrences says 'Forest::within builds a forest within another limit'. That is meaningless to a web or command-line user; the command rewrites it, a wasm client would not.

taste.title: Statistics counters change meaning with the engine
taste.note: For the Horn engine, nodes, memo_hits and memo_entries count markings. This is documented, and `engine` sits beside the counters in the JSON, but named fields per engine (R9's 'new fields rather than new meanings') would read better.

taste.title: Link-time optimisation helps the renderers much and the searches little
taste.note: No `[profile.release]` sets `lto` or `codegen-units`. Counted with a build of `--config profile.ltoaudit.{inherits=release, lto=fat, codegen-units=1}` (target/audit/ltoaudit, 40 s to build): derivation-chain-64 −18.4 %, render-typst −20.6 %, render-latex −15.4 %, read-json −8.3 %, ordinary-pigeons −8.0 %, search-wide-m2-256 −6.9 %, render-svg −5.5 %, but the focused searches only −1.2 % (chain-128) to −3.6 % (qbf/20#2) and additive −0.1 %. Report 15 measured 1–6 % CPU on searches and set it aside; the search gains stay within the few percent stage 0 says a count cannot settle. The author's call on build time against the export paths.

taste.title: The checker allocates a boxed state and fresh hash tables per node
taste.note: check-qbf-20-2: `__rust_alloc` 9.27 M, `__rust_dealloc` 11.0 M, table set-up in `reserve_rehash`/`fallible_with_capacity` about 10 M of 135.6 M Ir (about 22 %); `Pass::just` allocates a `Box<State>` and a table per leaf (30,720 calls). A pool of cleared states would remove most of it, but it must keep the memory account exact (`most`), the checker's journeys are the ones whose counts do not track time, and the check is 0.3 % of search time on the target set: not worth a finding.

taste.title: The tally of a stable sequent is summed again from every member's row
taste.note: `Tally::add` is 23.1 % of search-qbf-20-2 (1,259,900 calls, about 121 Ir each) and 12.1 % of partition-no-5. Carrying a tally down from the parent would cost a copy of `row_atoms` sums per premise, about what the recount costs on qbf, so no proportionate fix is evident beyond the per-copy case in the member-list finding.

taste.title: The additive path's memo grows by rehashing
taste.note: `reserve_rehash` of `HashMap<(OccId, OccId), Option<NodeId>>` is 12.5 % of search-additive-14 (74.5 M Ir). Amortised doubling up to the 2²⁰-entry cap; a reserve up front would charge tens of MB to problems that need few pairs. Left as it is unless a target asks.

taste.title: The LLTP and TPTP readers collect every line into a Vec<char>
taste.note: `let chars: Vec<char> = before.chars().collect();` per line: 4.25 % of read-lltp, 4.0 % of read-tptp. A byte-level scan (the names it looks for are ASCII) would do without the allocation; small.

taste.title: The text tree's gap is outside the size bound
taste.note: `gap: u16` up to 65 535 columns, whose spaces 'the bound on a derivation's size does not count'. `--style text.gap=65535` on a wide derivation under the default view bound can write gigabytes of spaces (interact's `show` builds them in a String). This is documented, and Ctrl-C stops it. Counting `gap × premises` in `Size::bytes`, or a lower cap, would close it.

taste.title: The input text has no size bound
taste.note: `read` uses `read_to_string` on a file or standard input of any size. `--occurrence-limit` applies only after the parse, whose memory is linear in the text, so `--file /dev/zero` reads until memory runs out (under a time limit the load thread is abandoned, not stopped). A byte cap tied to the occurrence limit would make the flag a bound on input memory too.

taste.title: Chumsky-era fields in ParseError
taste.note: `label` and `expected` are always empty since the hand-written parser replaced chumsky. Either fill them (see the finding) or remove them before 0.1.0 (D18).

taste.title: Found::proved and Found::failed duplicate the variants
taste.note: Thirty call sites use the lower-case constructors, while `after`, `map` and the patterns use `Found::Proved`/`Failed` directly. One spelling would read better.

taste.title: Rules::stack always equals Rules::exponentials
taste.note: `stack: exponentials` is the only assignment. Two names for one fact make a reader wonder whether they can differ; a doc line or a method `loop_check()` would say it.

taste.title: initial returns Step but never fails
taste.note: clippy::unnecessary_wraps. Every path returns Ok, and the callers' `?` is dead.

taste.title: focus_class orders candidates by a bare u8 0..3
taste.note: An enum with derived Ord (Alone, Forced, Plus, Free) would name the four classes the doc lists.

taste.title: remember repeats the collect-and-insert block
taste.note: The two blocks differ only in `tight`. A loop over [false, true] or a helper would show the escalation once.

taste.title: Tuple variants with unnamed numbers in Stop
taste.note: `Turn(_, u64)` and `Slice(_, u64, u64)` hold the work left and the slice. Struct variants would name them.

taste.title: Runtime::new is pub(crate) although the rules require Lent::take
taste.note: Its only caller is Lent::take in the same file. Making it private would enforce core-parallel.md's "never Runtime::new".

taste.title: Test helpers repeated across the engines' test modules
taste.note: `decided` (here and focus/parallel.rs:542), `run`/`provable` (focus/tests.rs:42 and 72, net.rs:519 and 554) and `mode_for` (focus/tests.rs:1080, net.rs:563) could live in the test-only generate.rs. The two `classic_sequents` tables share 12 of the net's 21 sequents.

taste.title: Baton::pass and pass_polling repeat the hand-off
taste.note: The locked check of stop/ended, setting the holder and notify_all are written twice.

taste.title: Pooled derefs to Vec
taste.note: A crate-private convenience. C-DEREF applies only to the public surface, but a wrapper whose settle() must be called on give-back invites using it as a plain Vec.

taste.title: Redundant zero test in Shared::new
taste.note: `if limit == 0 { 0 } else { per_shard }`: per_shard is already 0 when limit is 0.

taste.title: one_of_each_copy recomputes set_bytes inline
taste.note: A borrow of by_class prevents the method call; computing `self.set_bytes()` before taking the borrow would remove the copy of the formula.

taste.title: The exports' String functions and write twins could be one generic call, but cost little as they are
taste.note: Each target has `derivation(&Derivation, &Options) -> String` (a three-line wrapper over `write` with `|| false`), `write` for a linear derivation and `ordinary` for an LK/LJ one (latex.rs:353-388, typst.rs:301-335, svg/mod.rs:570-620, rocq.rs:530-625), while the text tree is a method on both derivation types. A public sealed trait (today's crate-private `Drawn`) would make one `write<D>` per target and drop `ordinary`; but the wrappers are one-liners forwarding to one generic `tree`, so nothing drifts, and Rocq's ordinary certificate is a different writer anyway. Asymmetry worth noting: the linear derivation has a String form, the ordinary one does not.

taste.title: Three tree layouts implement one algorithm with slightly different bar rules
taste.note: proofs/fmt.rs::layout (bar = max(conclusion, span) centred), export/svg/tree.rs::draw (bar = union of span and conclusion) and the Typst script LAYOUT (typst.rs:377, as the SVG). Unifying text and SVG over a width measure would change one output (snapshots), so it is the author's choice whether one look is wanted.

taste.title: JSON format tests in core/tests/serialize.rs overlap the behaviour lock
taste.note: json_format, outcome_json_format, net_json_format_and_round_trip and interactive_json_format_and_round_trip pin exact strings that core/tests/lock.rs's corpus also pins for similar inputs, so a deliberate format change is blessed in json.txt and edited by hand here. core-sequents.md describes both as intended; trimming serialize.rs to round trips and rejections is a possible simplification.

taste.title: Index newtypes repeat the same three methods
taste.note: TermId, Atom, OccId, NodeId and InfId each define new/get/index by hand; a small macro or a generic `Id<T>` would state it once. Purely cosmetic.

taste.title: `_with` and `_within` suffixes mean different things
taste.note: `derivation_with(&view, stop)` takes options and a stop, `check_within(mode, memory)`, `derivation_size_within(.., memory)`, `Forest::within(&sequent, limit)` and `mist::read_within` take a bound. Consistent within each family, but a reader must learn both.

taste.title: lltp::HYPHEN and DOT are spelt out again in the LaTeX escaper
taste.note: `'‿' => {\smallsmile}`, `'·' => {\cdotp}` with a comment that `lltp` needs `parse`; moving the two constants to an always-compiled place would let the escaper name them.

taste.title: prove.rs mixes five concerns
taste.note: The file is 1 337 lines: the race, the output policy (`Show`, `Shown`, `Prefixed`), the derivation/net/render writers, the user-facing message builders (`too_large`, `unfit`, `over_memory`, `unknown`, `statistics`) and `check`. Natural seams: race → library, `output.rs`, `messages.rs`, `check.rs`.

taste.title: Help text hard-codes values that library constants name
taste.note: "NanoYalla 1.1.3" duplicates `export::rocq::NANOYALLA`, and "a tree up to nine inferences high" (line 895) duplicates `typst::CURRYST_HEIGHT`. clap doc comments cannot interpolate them, but `#[arg(long_help = ...)]` built from the constants, or a test comparing the two, would keep them in step.

taste.title: `Deadline::within` and `detached` are the same spawn-and-wait
taste.note: Both spawn a named thread with `LOAD_STACK` and send a result over a channel, then on `Disconnected` join and resume the panic. They differ only in the wait (one deadline against a poll). One helper with a wait strategy would do.

taste.title: `net_into` takes eight arguments and `derivation` seven
taste.note: `net_into` has `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`, and `derivation` takes seven. `halt`, `why`, `prefix` and `out` are threaded by hand through prove, batch, interact and ordinary; a small context struct would carry them.

taste.title: Two unit tables for byte sizes
taste.note: `bytes_text` has its own [B…EiB] table and argument_parsing.rs:1005 `UNITS` has [B…TiB]. `Limit`'s Display and `bytes_text` format sizes two ways ("1GiB" against "1.0 GiB").

taste.title: The fuzz target list is written three times
taste.note: The targets are listed in fuzz/run.sh:27, fuzz/seed.sh:124 and the [[bin]] entries of fuzz/Cargo.toml. run.sh could read them with `cargo fuzz list`.

taste.title: cli/Cargo.toml names default features of linlog explicitly
taste.note: `interactive`, `latex`, `rocq`, `svg` and `typst` are already defaults. Listing them is harmless and documents intent, but it reads as if `parse` and `serialize` were not used.

taste.title: counts-against-time.py parses the ratchet's Markdown table with a regex
taste.note: The ratchet's printed table is an interface here. A `--csv` output of `ratchet` would be sturdier.

taste.title: A Mode struct literal beside the named constant
taste.note: `search_spec` spells intuitionistic affine as a struct literal, where problems.rs uses `Mode::INTUITIONISTIC.affine()`. R51 asks for Mode to be built without struct literals.

taste.title: History in comments
taste.note: Several comments state what was before rather than why the code is as it is now: split.rs:385 "which a tensor … used to run out of", memo.rs Memo doc "a full memo of a gibibyte went in half a second when every key was two allocations", reach.rs:43 "a count of work instead started it after a few expansions", schedule.rs:97 and 171 "the search the default ran alone before" / "the one Auto ran alone before", split.rs:239 "moving the whole search … was a tenth of a net's time". A5 allows the measured reason. A rewrite in the present ("recursing costs a level per link", "an allocation per key made freeing slow") would read better.

taste.title: Stop's tuple variants carry unnamed counters
taste.note: `Stop::Turn(&mut dyn FnMut() -> bool, u64)` and `Stop::Slice(&mut dyn FnMut(bool) -> bool, u64, u64)` say in prose which u64 is the work left and which the slice length ("the last field"). Named fields (`left`, `slice`) would say it in the type.

taste.title: Options has one getter named unlike its setter
taste.note: Every option is set by a method named after it (`jobs`, `copies`, …). The one getter is `job_count`, because `jobs` is the setter. A front end that needs the other values cannot read them. Either a getter per option under another convention, or none.

taste.title: The dispatch table's Horn row is a paragraph
taste.note: The "measured" cell of the Horn row in Engine's docs runs to about 250 words in one table cell, which rustdoc renders as a very tall cell. The measurements could follow the table as a paragraph under the row's engine.

taste.title: text_size returns an unnamed pair
taste.note: `Derivation::text_size(&self, options) -> (usize, usize)` returns width and lines as a tuple. A small struct with `width` and `lines` (or reusing `Size`'s field names) would be clearer at the call sites.

taste.title: Atom and variable both name one concept
taste.note: The type is Atom and the accessor atom_names, but the variants are Term::Var/DualVar, Kind::Var/DualVar, Sign::Var/DualVar, the error InvalidVariableIndex and the JSON var_dict/V/D. Both are domain words (Atom's doc says 'an atom (a propositional variable)'); a rename of the Rust items is broad and the JSON keys are locked, so this is put to the author rather than counted.

taste.title: The harness spells 'no bound' two ways
taste.note: linlog-bench run takes `--copies none` but `--memory-limit 0` for no bound, and the command takes `none` for both; one spelling would match the command.

taste.title: SVG font described two ways
taste.note: SequentFormat::Svg says 'set in the Euler Math font' while Format::Svg adds 'unless --style names another'; seq print takes --style svg.font too.

taste.title: Date::from_unix clamps silently with an odd phrase
taste.note: 'years past 65 535 are that year' reads as a tautology; 'are clamped to 65 535' says it.

taste.title: Imperative trait-method docs
taste.note: 'Write the term of an inference.' / 'Write text.' where the crate writes 'Writes …'.

taste.title: Duplicate row in the net engine's classic_sequents
taste.note: `("|- a, ~a, a, ~a", false)` appears twice in the first table (the second and the last row). The earlier assessment's other excess items (`search::tests::stop` equal to `net::tests::stop`, `focus::parallel::tests::agree`'s second assertion) no longer hold: the two stop tests now differ (poll count and node count vs a plain `|| true`), and `classic_sequents` pins textbook verdicts independently of the focused engine.

taste.title: The tree of `A, A -o B |- B` is printed in five doc examples
taste.note: lib.rs:35, proofs/mod.rs:285, search/mod.rs:138, proofs/derivation.rs:623 and an interactive test pin the same text. As doctests they serve the manual (C-EXAMPLE), so this is a preference, not excess.

taste.title: Earlier test gaps from plan/reports/17-assessment.md section 1.4 that are now closed
taste.note: Checked against the code: all 34 rule labels are compiled by `every_label` (core/tests/export.rs:241); `Rule::from_str(rule.name())` round trip is `names_round_trip` (proofs/style.rs); parse error positions are `error_positions` (core/tests/parse.rs:154); a stop in a forced chain is `stops_inside_a_forced_chain` (focus/tests.rs:657); the focused memo with a small limit is `bounded_failures` and `full_and_emptied` (memo.rs); `chains` is tested directly with negatives (focus/tests.rs:1407); `prove_goal` off the roots is `goals` (search/mod.rs:1874); depth.rs now includes the ordinary layer. Still open from that list: nothing large goes through `check` except the synthetic `shared()` proofs and depth.rs.

taste.title: readme.rs compares output only, not the exit status that README states
taste.note: README line 901 ('so this one is 2') and 410 state statuses; run() discards `out.status`. A `$ cmd  # exit 2` marker would pin them, but the lock and cli.rs already pin the statuses of the same commands, so this is a preference.

taste.title: Lock case name `error-memory-limit` has status 3 (unknown), not an error
taste.note: Its file reads `--- status 3` and an `unknown (LL, ...)` line; `refuse-memory-limit` or `unknown-memory-limit` would say what the pinned call is. Renaming moves a file of the lock, hence a commit of its own.

taste.title: every_style_option spawns three processes per row of a 60-row table
taste.note: It takes 0.75 s, so there is no cost to argue; whether the library's own style tests already pin each option's effect and this table need only prove the `--style`/`--style-file` plumbing once per format is a choice of the author.

taste.title: An `unknown` line recommends raising a limit that will not decide the sequent
taste.note: `linlog prove -q --jobs 2 --timeout 3s "!(A + B) |- !A + !B"` prints `unknown (LL, classical, focus engine): the recursion limit of 2048 was reached after 633.88ms at a copy bound of 511; raise it with --recursion-limit N` (exit 3). The usability baseline (story 14) wants advice that says when more resources will not help. R138's text concerns another case, so this is the author's decision.

taste.title: README gives the size of the largest LLTP problem as 86 MB
taste.note: README 321-322: `the largest problem of the LLTP library, a file of 86 MB`; bench.md says 103 MB, and the three `SYJ212+1.020.p` files in bench/lltp measure 76.6 MB (cbn), 95.4 MB (cbv) and 103.3 MB (01). plan/reports/23 mentions an 86 MB split text file; the block is skipped by the README test, so nothing checks the figure.

taste.title: Rules files cite plan steps and panels as history
taste.note: cli.md:292 `a panel of step 27 found`, cli.md:193 `at the review of step 24`, bench.md `the step 14 report`: allowed in .claude/ (exempt from the conventions check), but CLAUDE.md asks comments to make sense from inside the repository.

taste.title: CLAUDE.md `the CLI enables the last eight` reads as a count over the list before it
taste.note: cli/Cargo.toml names eight features explicitly (interactive, latex, parallel, pdf, png, rocq, svg, typst) and leaves default features on, so it enables all ten; the sentence is true only of the manifest's list.

taste.title: `Tally::judged` counts runs that answered `Unknown`
taste.note: The field is documented as "The engines' runs that answered beside a reference that decided" and is incremented (762) for every outcome, `Unknown` included; it appears only in assertion messages, so no test asserts that any engine ever decides a judged case. Counting the runs whose verdict was decided, or naming the field `answered`, would make the message say what it counts.

taste.title: The Mix enumeration yields each partition twice and counts the trivial ones as visits
taste.note: `splits(sequent)` under Mix gives every ordered pair `(left, right)` and its mirror, and `self.visit()` (414) is charged before the `is_empty` skip (417), so a Mix sequent of `n` members spends `2ⁿ` visits where `2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1` partitions are distinct, which brings `VISITS` nearer on the larger generated Mix cases. Fixing the first member on the left, as the engine does, halves it; test-only, so a preference.

taste.title: `two_sided` allocates its key before the memo lookup
taste.note: `let key = (hypotheses.to_vec(), goal)` is built on every call, hits included; `one_sided` (309) looks up by slice and copies only on insert. Test-only, so a preference.

taste.title: Rocq's ⊗ splits the goal with a linear search and remove per formula
taste.note: `left.iter().position(..)` and `left.remove(i)` inside the loop over `goal` make each ⊗ cost O(|goal|·|left|). Measured on left-nested chains `a1..an ⊢ a1 ⊗ … ⊗ an`: from n=1000 to n=2000, Rocq went from 0.21 s to 1.03 s (×4.9), LaTeX from 0.11 s to 0.43 s (×3.9). The output itself is quadratic, so the cubic term is small. A multiset count would make it linear, but the gain is unmeasured on any journey.

taste.title: pdf::Date's fields are unchecked
taste.note: Month, day, hour, minute and second are public u8 fields read from JSON. krilla clamps them (krilla-0.8.2 src/interchange/metadata.rs:340-371), so 2026-02-31 25:99 becomes a valid-looking date, silently. There is no panic. A `Date::new` that refuses would be cleaner.

taste.title: The tree's second walk asks no stop
taste.note: The position pass (163-170) is linear and cheap, and the passes around it poll. Polling in it too would make every walk of `draw` uniform. It is not a defect.

taste.title: classic_sequents written twice is not literally a duplicate, but ten rows are
taste.note: net.rs:574 and focus/tests.rs:83 share ten sequents with the same expected value (|- ~a, a; a |- a; |- a, a; |-; a * b |- a * b; |- a * b, ~a par ~b; |- a * b, ~a, ~b; |- a par b, ~a, ~b; |- (a * b) par (~a * ~b); a, a -o b, b -o c |- c; a -o b, b -o c |- a -o c; a -o b |- b -o a is 12 with the last two). The differential test samples only generated provable, mutated, doubled and balanced sequents, never these hand-written ones, so the net list is the net engine's only textbook ground truth; its `run` also checks the net and the from_proof round trip (net.rs:~530), which the focus `run` does not. Each list also has rows the other lacks (focus: additives and units; net: Mix, doubled conclusions). Not excess by S7. If one wants a single table, a shared `const CLASSIC` in search::tests run under each forced engine would write the twelve rows once; a preference, not a defect.

taste.title: search::tests::stop and net::tests::stop are not equal; the step-17 claim no longer holds
taste.note: mod.rs:1954 goes through prove_until with the dispatch and stops on the first poll, asserting the Verdict::Unknown mapping and the only test of the Display string of Reason::Stopped (the CLI prints its own time-limit text); net.rs:682 calls the engine directly and pins the poll cadence (nodes == 2, links == 1, no net). Focus `limits` (focus/tests.rs:227) and interactive.rs:1517 stop other paths. If anything is merged, it is the Display assertion into a test of all five Reason phrases (only CopyBound is asserted elsewhere, in copy_bound); the two stop tests stay.

taste.title: focus `limits` bundles five unrelated behaviours under one name
taste.note: limits (:211-292) checks the stop reason, RecursionLimit, that a `?` costs no level (3 000 of them), that tensor chains of 2 500 prove on the default stack, and a free split over 126 formulas. A failure names none of them. The chain checks use the same two shapes as `stops_inside_a_forced_chain` (:657, 5 000 factors) and wide-chain `a_chain_of_free_splits_costs_one_level` (:1461). Splitting it into one test per behaviour is a preference; nothing is unpinned or doubly pinned except the shapes.

taste.title: exponential_derivations renders trees that derivation.rs already pins
taste.note: Two of its five trees (`!A, !(A -o B) |- !B` and the affine `A, B |- A` weakening) are the same text as proofs/derivation.rs:~1615 and :~1648, there from hand-built proofs. The focus test additionally pins that the engine's own proofs unfold to those trees (the engine's choice of axiom orientation and copy order), which derivation.rs does not, so the test stays; only the overlap of rendering is double.

taste.title: The 'too many occurrences' message suggests Forest::within for a parse refusal
taste.note: For the parser, `TooManyOccurrences` reports `most + 1` and advises 'Forest::within builds a forest within another limit, of at most MOST'. A text refused at Forest::MOST cannot be read through Forest::within at all, so the advice does not apply to this caller. It matters only once a parse_within exists (finding 1), when the limit there is the caller's own.

taste.title: Inference::times is still a public field, but no separate finding
taste.note: Not fixed. `pub times: u32` sits on `Inference`, a struct whose fields are all public and which has no `#[non_exhaustive]` (:541-560). The reason it matters is that adding the field broke every literal and the next field will too. That is R50, whose evidence names Inference, and so ready-b-1. The member type of `sequent` is ready-b-3. Callers cannot break any invariant: Derivation and Interactive hand out only `&Inference`, `Derivation::from_parts` is crate-private, and the session's JSON does not carry `times` (serialize/interactive.rs:82 sets 1). What is left is small. Six struct literals set every field: derivation.rs:1127 and :1135, interactive.rs:227, :570 and :909, serialize/interactive.rs:77. Three of them are the same open leaf with `times: 1`. A crate-private constructor such as `Inference::open(sequent)` would make the next field one edit.

taste.title: Compact is still re-exported at the crate root, while the root's own items' companion types are not
taste.note: Not fixed. `linlog::Compact` is also reachable as `proofs::Compact` and `proofs::derivation::Compact`. At the root it is an adjective that does not say what it compacts; it is read only as the type of `ViewOptions::compact`. Meanwhile some types that root items need are not at the root: `UnknownRule`, the `FromStr` error of the root's `Rule`, and `Problem`, `Described` and `Dyadic`, which `CheckError`'s public field and `describe` return, live only under `proofs::`. One rule for the root (the common path and what its items return) would either move `Compact` down or rename it (for example `CompactView`).

taste.title: Text tree widths count code points, so wide or combining characters in atom names misalign the tree
taste.note: `Count::write_str` adds `s.chars().count()`, and the layout assumes one column per character ('every symbol used is one column'). That holds for the symbols, but atom names are user identifiers (unicode-ident), and a CJK or combining-mark name shifts bars and centring. A width table such as unicode-width would fix it at the cost of a dependency; this is noted only as a choice.

taste.title: Two functions named `unfold` with different jobs
taste.note: The free `unfold` (:729) runs the whole translation (size, record pass, build), while `Build::unfold` (:1187) plans one node, and `Task::Unfold` is a third use of the word. A name such as `translate`/`derive` for the free function would let a reader tell them apart.

taste.title: `Task::Infer { premises: 1, times: 1, principal: Some(..) }` written by hand beside the helper `from`
taste.note: `Copy`'s contraction (:1261-1267) and `weaken_run` (:1408-1415) build the one-premise `Infer` literal that `from` (:1172) exists to build. A helper `infer_one(sequent, rule, principal, times)` would make it one place.

taste.title: `split` clones the node's standard sequent only to take a difference
taste.note: `let extra = actual.difference(&self.standard(id));` clones the recorded Multiset (`Build::standard` returns a clone, :1008-1010), though `difference` takes a reference. Borrowing `&self.record.standard[&id]` avoids the copy. This is unmeasured, so it is listed as taste.

taste.title: Rules files carry history that a session cannot use and that points at plan files
taste.note: core-focus.md 893 ("until step 26, one thread's proofs carried the cuts ..."), core-parallel.md 176 (the same sentence again), core-horn.md 68 and 216 ("step 27's report", "the panel"), core-nets.md 211 ("plan/later.md"), core-ordinary.md ("plan/reports/25-ordinary-logic.md") narrate how the work was organised, which CLAUDE.md forbids in code comments; .claude/ is exempt from the machine check, so this is a style choice. The same cut-carrying story appears in two files and will drift.

taste.title: core-focus.md is 62 KB and loads whole for any read of a file under search/focus/
taste.note: About 16 000 tokens per session that touches the engine, most of it measurement narrative (before/after counts of every past optimisation). A split along the file's own seams (bias and memo contract; splits and counts; the default bias's two searches, which schedule.rs and parallel.rs readers need) would load less per task. Not a correctness matter.

taste.title: core-horn.md states that `microlp` "reads a clock"
taste.note: Line 333 gives a reason against a dependency from the crate's source; I did not read microlp (no network, not vendored here), so the claim is unverified. It is a rejected-alternative note, not an instruction.

taste.title: Options::stack_size has two explanations for its doubling
taste.note: The method doc (line 1171-1173) says the per-level cost is "doubled for the derivation built from the proof"; the constant's doc (1178-1181) and core-focus.md 838-840 say the doubling is a margin over the measured stack per level. Cli.md says "twice the engine's measured cost per level". Same number, different reasons.

taste.title: The --isolate child writes its record with println!, which panics on a closed pipe
taste.note: `one` uses `println!("{}", done.text)`. If the parent has died, this panics (exit 101) where every other writer returns an error. The parent normally reads the pipe, so a user cannot reach it. Write it through `io::write(None, …)` so that every path handles a write error the same way.

taste.title: Hash collision guard in the marking table has no seam to test it
taste.note: `self.hashes[e] == hash && bytes == *written` -> `||` survives because a 64-bit collision cannot be made by a test; with a collision the marking is dropped as seen and an exhaustion would be a false refutation (probability about n^2/2^65, 4e-5 for 4e7 markings). A cfg(test) hash mask would pin it; I leave the decision (production code for a test) to the author. `hash -> 0/1` (550) is correct but quadratic and no test notices.

taste.title: Two numeric bounds are argued in comments but not pinned
taste.note: `Bag::MOST = u32::MAX - 1` (check.rs:147) and `reach::MOST_MARKINGS = u32::MAX as usize - 1` (reach.rs:35) survive `-` -> `/`: no test can build 4 billion members. A `const _: () = assert!(Bag::MOST < u32::MAX as usize);` and `assert!(MOST_MARKINGS + 1 <= u32::MAX as usize)` would pin both at compile time.

taste.title: The Kind::One arm of horn::head_of is dead for every sequent a reading admits
taste.note: The head is the last factor of the dual tensor, so it is popped before any `1`; deleting the arm changed nothing in 32 000 random intuitionistic nets with `1` in bodies. Keep it for symmetry with Reader::clause, or drop it as dead code.

taste.title: `derived` allocates and sorts a copy of `facts.shared` at every `⊗` and Mix
taste.note: `let mut shared: Vec<OccId> = facts.shared.to_vec(); shared.sort_unstable();` is one allocation per two-premise node of the size pass, uncounted against the bound (bounded by a zone, as the rules say). The checker's `Pass::shared` could be sorted in place once before `derived` is called, and the observer would read a sorted slice. The size pass is not a journey, so this is unmeasured (A1's taste row).

taste.title: `weights()` and `afford` each run twice for a compact view
taste.note: `measured` calls `check::afford` (size.rs:543) and `examine` calls it again with the same numbers (check.rs:738); `size::weights(proof.forest())` is computed in `measured` (size.rs:547), dropped, and computed again for `Held` (derivation.rs:792). Returning the weights beside `Firm` would save one pass over the forest per compact view.

taste.title: The used-`?` arm copies the premise's `Sub` wholesale, resting on three silent equalities
taste.note: `Quest(_, p) if facts.used => Sub { ..at(p) }` keeps the premise's `weight`, `goal` and `absorbs` instead of the node's own `sub` fields; they are equal today (the `?` step moves `weight(o)` from `unrestricted` to `linear`, `?` formulas are never outputs, `any` is untouched), but `Sub { weight: sub.weight, goal: sub.goal, absorbs: sub.absorbs, ..at(p) }` would say what is relied on, and a debug assertion would catch a checker change that breaks it.

taste.title: `unfold` reserves the whole derivation up front when both bounds are lifted
taste.note: `Vec::with_capacity(size.inferences as usize)` asks the allocator for up to `Derivation::MOST` inferences at once before the first node is built; with `UNBOUNDED.memory(None)` on a tower(31) proof that is a 170 GB reservation (an abort under a cgroup limit, a lazily backed mapping with overcommit) where a gradual growth would be ended by the stop or the bound. Outside this gap's file; the caller asked for no bound, so a preference only.

taste.title: prove-mall-units pins an atom named T, which reads like top
taste.note: `call("prove-mall-units", &["prove", "|- T, 0 + 1"])` pins `unprovable … T occurs 1 more time than ~T`. The syntax spells the unit `top`/`⊤`, so `T` is an atom, and the case pins no ⊤ at all. If ⊤ was meant, the sequent is provable and the case pins the wrong thing. If the atom was meant, a different name would avoid the misreading.

taste.title: The two 'valid proof' lines differ, and interact's `proof --json` prints a prose line before the JSON
taste.note: `check` prints `valid proof of ⊢ … (classical)` (check-valid.txt), while interact's `proof` prints `valid proof (classical)` (interact-session.txt, README). With `--json` that line comes before the JSON object on standard output, so a script cutting the JSON out of a transcript must skip it. Taste for a dialogue; one wording for both would read better.

taste.title: The ordinary Rocq certificate ends with an extra blank line
taste.note: ordinary-rocq.txt ends `Qed.` followed by an empty line, while format-rocq.txt and format-rocq-standalone.txt end at `Qed.`. A trailing-newline difference between the two Rocq printers.

taste.title: `seq print -i` rewrites the right side by commutativity
taste.note: `seq print -i 'A * B -o C |- ~C -o ~(A * B)'` prints `(A ⊗ B) ⊸ C` on the right; also `A |- ~C -o ~A` prints `A ⊢ A ⊸ C`. The help says it 'prints as … again', which is true of its example. A user may still not expect the contrapositive to turn into a different-looking formula; one sentence in the help would say why.

taste.title: reference.rs's intuitionistic differential test never mutates the goal
taste.note: `generate::mutate(&mut rng, &mut hypotheses, 3)` leaves the goal intact, and returns false for the 11-17 % of samples with no hypotheses, so the independent prover never sees a mutant whose output-position literal changed. focus/tests.rs generated_ill and the default-bias test push the goal into the list first, as they should. Probably worth copying that line, but the engines treat the two positions symmetrically in most prunes, so it is not defended as a finding.

taste.title: mutate's doc says it returns whether there was a literal; it also returns false when atoms < 2, and every caller passes 3
taste.note: The `atoms < 2` guard is never taken by any test, and the atom count is 3 in every call of provable, ill, mutate and balanced in core/src. No test varies it, so the engines' atom ranks and rank gaps are never seen at 1, 2 or 4+ atoms. A one-line doc fix, or a loop over atoms in one test.

taste.title: Budgets are nominal: the leaf choice ignores the budget and the process is near critical
taste.note: At budgets 2..10 84 % of unit-free MLL samples have under 10 occurrences (mean 5.4, mean 2.2 conclusion formulas) and 12 % to 37 % of the other sets have four or more formulas. Budgets 2..24 raise the share of 20-80 occurrence samples only to 6 %. The shapes the prunes need do occur at the tests' sizes: ⊤ under an exponential 14-26 % of the additive+exponential samples, an atom both inside and outside an exponential 16-36 %, top-level duplicates 3-15 %, a promotion with ?-context 2.7 %, essential affine weakening in 17 % of classical and 9 % of ILL mutants. The ignored `generated_large_sample` is the only sample that goes bigger (already a standing finding).

taste.title: `p` with one formula and no units, and `a` after a computed sub-proof, are budget-burning no-ops
taste.note: 548 of 3000 unit-free MLL samples end in the `par-noop` return, and IllGenerator::proof computes proof(budget-1) before a `b'a'` choice discards it. Harmless, but the drawn shapes are fewer than the budget suggests.

taste.title: The step-17 item 10 decision (a shared forest) is nowhere recorded; the code answers it: not needed before 0.1.0, and additive afterwards
taste.note: Every owner holds its own `Forest` by value: `Proof { forest: Forest, .. }` (proofs/mod.rs:309-314), `ProofStructure { forest: Forest, .. }` (nets/mod.rs:182-197), `Interactive { forest: Forest, .. }` (interactive.rs:198-208), each built by a by-value constructor (`Proof::new(forest: Forest, …)` :322, `ProofStructure::new(forest: Forest, mix)` :202, `Interactive::new(&Sequent)` :214) and read through `forest(&self) -> &Forest` (proofs/mod.rs:372, nets/mod.rs:293, interactive.rs:421); `Reading<'a>` and `Derivation<'a>` borrow one (reading.rs:186, derivation.rs:659-666). The clones are one per proof found (`Answer::of_arena`, search/mod.rs:450), one per net engine run and one per worker of its pool (net.rs:227 via :104, :903, :937), one per sequentialization (sequentialize.rs:37), one per `from_proof` (nets/mod.rs:258) and one per `Interactive::proof()` (:967): each O(n) beside an O(n) or larger piece of work, none on a journey, and the memory doc already says the forest, the proof returned and the net's structure are uncounted (search/mod.rs:975-988). Because the fields are private and the accessors return `&Forest`, an `Arc<Forest>` inside the three owners, a `Proof::into_parts` that gives the forest back, or an owned positions value for R81/R123 can all be added after 0.1.0 without breaking a signature (`Proof::new` keeps taking a `Forest` and wraps it); only turning `Reading<'a>` or `Derivation<'a>` into owned types would drop a lifetime parameter and break callers that name it, and no entry of the register asks for that (R4 allows a write-only derivation form; R81 allows recompute or an owned positions value). So the shared forest is no S16 finding; the one cost today that the ownership causes is the per-call reading above. R81's "State now" (requirements.md:713) and the step-17 item would be clearer if one of them recorded this: that sharing is additive and the owners' clones are documented as uncounted, so that no later step reopens the question.

taste.title: targets.sh header gives the run time as three quarters of an hour; bench.md says 35 minutes
taste.note: targets.sh:19-21 says 'about three quarters of an hour at the commit the first baseline measured'. bench.md:309-310 says 'About 35 minutes at the engines of the first baseline'. before.csv summed per stream gives about 36 minutes (stream 1) and 28 minutes (stream 2), so 35 is nearer. CLAUDE.md:89 says about 20 minutes for today's engine. The numbers are estimates, not claims about behaviour; one sentence in the script could simply match bench.md.

taste.title: README says the intuitionistic pass decides 2 047 problems within 5 s; RESULTS.md's 'Solved within the time limit' table counts 2 049
taste.note: The cause is ready-a-15: summary counts a verdict after the limit as solved. lltp-intuitionistic.csv has two Petri nets proved at 5.89 s and 5.76 s under a 5 s limit (GPPP_G-PPP-1000-100_5_1, GPPP_G-PPP-1000-10_5_1). README.md:1087-1089 and COMPARISON.md ('2 049 (2 late)') are right. Only RESULTS.md's heading and its solved column disagree, and they are generated. Fixing summary.rs fixes the heading; no separate edit is needed.

taste.title: format.sh keeps a second copy of treefmt's file types
taste.note: The suffix list (.rs .nix .toml .sh .envrc .py) repeats what modules/treefmt.nix's formatters include, and claude-infra.md:96-97 says the hook runs 'if modules/treefmt.nix formats its type'. treefmt already ignores a path that no formatter matches, so the filter could become 'under the root' alone, or be generated from treefmt's config. Today the two lists agree for every type in the tree.

taste.title: session-jj-state.sh reads $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, which claude-infra.md's hook rules say not to use
taste.note: claude-infra.md:124-126 says to read the payload's `cwd`, not $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, for the directory Claude works in, because the variable stays at the original checkout after Claude enters a worktree. The SessionStart hook does `cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}"`, so a compact or clear inside a worktree would print the original checkout's @. That only matters if worktrees are used with jj, so I list it here and not as a finding. The fix is either to read `cwd` from the payload or to narrow the rule to the PostToolUse hooks.
